analysis.name: Amir Sariri
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This is not an easy course but if you are willing to put in the work you'll get a lot out of it. He cares an incredible deal about student learning and will give you all the attention and time you need as long as you demonstrate genuine interest. Take only if you are seriously interested in learning the concepts and don't count on a high grade.

Amir tries to get students to participate in class. His lecture slides aren't copied from a textbook, so lecture is great. He also uses case studies to teach certain topics which was always helpful as it gave you real-life examples of the in-class material. The only thing is that there is a group project which is heavily weighted and no homework.

Not a super hard class. Find quizlets to help you study for the weekly proctored quizzes. As a person, he can be kind of rude but I found it challenging and forced me to learn. The group project seems hard but actually turns our to be beneficial for learning. This class doesnt require much of you but when it does you should put in the effort.

Not the greatest prof. Can be very blunt and mean to students when they don't know an answer. Proctored Quizzes every week and Exams are even worse. He's not very good at communicating either. Don't recommend taking this class with him. Should be an A or B but I'm struggling to even pull a C.
It seems like he's still figuring out how to teach the content, and the class felt all over the place.

analysis.name: Cari Ann Boersma
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Boersma is awesome. She makes an effort to foster a community in the class. You will become a much better speaker by the end of the class. As long as you participate and put effort into the assignments, you will do well. One of the most fun classes I've taken at this school.
She gave good feedback on my assignments and understood us as students. Also was very welcoming and everyone in my class liked her.

She made this class so fun by fostering a very nice community within the class. It was my favorite one this semester! Very presentation based, and you become way more comfortable presenting in front of the class by the end with feedback from her and your classmates. Just follow her instructions, and you'll be all set.

She is a very good COM teacher. She makes everything that we learn very relatable. The class focuses more on presentations with feedback from your peers. The class is pretty laid-back as long as you do what is required of you. She makes the class very fun!

Cari runs an easy yet fair class. as long as you do the quizzes and prepare a little for presentation you can get a A. The class atmosphere is lively, and I looked forward to going to class every day.

analysis.name: Michelle Albitz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: My opinion of Professor Albitz changed a ton throughout the semester. While she might be on the harder end of grading speeches, getting a good grade in her course is still very achievable. I found she genuinely cares about her students, and even though the course itself is a little flawed, I would still definitely recommend her section!

While she may be one of the "harder" comm graders, that's really exaggerating. I was not the best at speeches, but I averaged a 90 on them and didn't do much preparation. Lectures can be boring sometimes, but that's not her fault it's the department's fault. She truly cares about the students and gets to know them

Albitz is a great person, always bringing energy and good vibes to class. In terms of grading, I always felt it was very fair. There were clear rubrics, and I understood why points were lost on speeches. Also, she is very accessible if you have a question on a speech, project, or homework.

prof albitz is an understanding person, she is silly and easy to talk to. her classroom has an open and lighthearted vibe. she is more of a tough grader and i would say you definitely need to put in effort to get a good grade on your speeches, but the rubric is pretty clear.

Pretty good overall, I have no complaints. I do think the grading is slightly harder than it should be for a COM class but she's good at what she does. An A is still easily achievable for the most part.

analysis.name: Andres Posada
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 99 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He explains things well but the course management is awful. The first midterm has 20+ pages of FRQ in 60 min. Projects were not that hard but the handouts created lots of confusion which made them harder than supposed to. TAs were not responding on Campuswire. A question can be left unanswered for a week until someone else in the class answer it.

TA is not helpful and has slow replies on the campuswire, even if they reply to the post, the answer sometimes is unhelpful or wrong. The professor curves the class differently, he literally lowers the standard of C a lot and only a little curve is given to A and B(got 83 pre-curve and left with a B). 25 free response questions in 1st exam.

Great communicator and teacher, very funny. Very demanding of students but for a tough class, it means we are up to date on the material. Cares enough to answer questions patiently and brings complicated ideas like data structures to life with well explained diagrams. The subject material is by nature difficult but he makes the most of it.

Professor Bejarano made CS25100 engaging with humor and care. He simplifies complex DSA topics while offering invaluable career advice for the real world. More than a teacher, he is a mentor who fosters open discussion and genuinely invests in student success. His support and expertise make him an exceptional, must-take instructor.

One of the best lecturers at Purdue: he cares a lot about our learning and will go at good pace where we can take notes AND understand what is going on. Homework/projects are a lot of work, but they are very fair and TAs can help. Midterms/Finals were all MCQs so it isn't hard to do well (C/B) but it can be quite hard to get an A/A- as no curve.

analysis.name: Andy Hudmon
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: lectures are very easy to understand. you will leave lecture feeling like you understand what is going on instead of studying for hours trying to figure out what the bullet points are saying. very concise and engaging
He is very funny and cares about his students' success. Biochem is a hard class, but he tries to make sure you understand the concepts and is very accessible outside of class.

Dr. Hudmon is the one redeemable factor in this mess of a class. He works hard to make sure we are understanding his material, which can be difficult at times. However, his exams are extremely fair in comparison to Krusemark's and he pulls directly from the slides. Exam review sessions are helpful, given he actually answers questions unlike others.

Hudmon seems to really care about his students and explains lecture in way for us to understand. His exam questions come straight from the slides or iClicker questions. He emphasized important information that we needed to know (like for homework or exams). He rarely fell behind in slides and if he ever did, he made extra videos to compensate.

Dr. Hudmon is the only reason this class is bearable. His lectures are much easier to follow and he takes time to ensure we are understanding the material. Exam content is pulled straight from the slides and he will even recycle past exam questions. If he was the course coordinator rather than Krusemark, student performance would be way better.

analysis.name: Andres Vargas
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 116 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He 's very helpful in class and at office hours. You do not need a textbook if you attend lectures and use slides. You should probably practice his problem sets a lot, I didn't realize this till the final, so don't be like me. Hotseat points boost grades ideally by a letter grade and his exams are pretty difficult since there are no sample exams.

Take his class, seriously! A good professor, very helpful !!!!!! His lectures and slides are easy to understand and helpful enough. No need to buy the textbook. And also, he took participation points. Exams are moderate, and getting A's for exams is not that hard. It's all multiple choice questions. If you do all the homework, it's A in your hand!

Vargas is an incredible professor. In addition to teaching very well, he uses third-party elements (e.g., news clips) to enhance his lectures. The class is not difficult; he gives extra credit for merely showing up to class (very generous), and the hw/practices exams are exactly like the exams  very approachable guy & knowledgeable.

Dr Vargas is one of the greatest economics professors and lectures I've had! he is super kind and very helpful. His lectures are well organized with lots of examples and always willing to answer questions before, during, and after class. I've had him for macro too and although the topics can be quiet hard he can help you through understanding well!

This was an ok professor, but his lectures are basically him reading presentations. He doesn't make content easy, and I would learn the same amount of things through the textbook or youtube. He says attendance isn't mandatory, but uses iClicker for points. Not the best if you want to be genuinely engaged during lectures.

analysis.name: Anson Soderbery
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Soderbery somehow gets paid $170,000/year to confuse a lecture hall full of 70 students. This professor is truly living the dream. Going to his lectures will make it seem like you're in an art class with the number of turtles, squirrels, and acorns you'll be drawing on your attendance sheet from not knowing what is going on.

Lectures were very informative. The sheet questions he asked encourages low stakes participation as they weren't graded for accuracy. The homeworks were good preparation for the exams. Exams were a lot of writing, but fair given what he said would be on the exams. He is very fair with policies regarding grading. Would recommend, only teaches Fall

Was a really funny professor who taught me the most about economics of all my professors. Loves to engage with students and has a lot of time for real world discussions of his concepts outside of class. Overall loved his lectures and looked forward to them every day. He also breaks a lot preconceived ideas, encouraged us to think for ourselves.

Professor Soderbery is very kind and funny. Some lectures can be quiet boring but he always wants to engage in discussions with students, although this could be fun there was one person who kept asking or answering questions which got pretty annoying but overall a good and fun class.  He is pretty hard to access outside of class.

Do not bother showing up to the TA review sessions. Their explanations to the topic were far from coherent and understandable it was laughable. After the first exam which I did poorly on I stopped listening even though he's a funny guy. Relied almost solely on the textbook for the last 2 exams and got a high B/low A on them.

analysis.name: Mark Ailor
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Ailor has got to be the best professor at Purdue University. Not only is this man fair, caring, hilarious, but he is a sensation. Give this guy a raise because I promise he is the most liked and respected professor to ever walk into this institution. Id nominate this guy for an Oscar. If you see him walking around thank him for existing.

Professor Ailor is great! He is extremely engaging during his lectures and cares about his students! He always makes sure to address questions when there is challenging material. He has a great sense of humor that makes his lectures so much more enjoyable! He is very clear with expectations!
Love him, he is a great professor and so funny. He is so fun to talk to! He is straightforward with expectations.

Professor Ailor makes learning fun and it's easy to remember what he teaches. Prepare to take notes though! He will exam you on the details he mentions (that aren't written on the slides). He's also very down to earth and humble, and will use his own experiences to help students understand what he's teaching.
God took his time with this man

analysis.name: Abigail Banan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 66 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lectures aren't great, Professor Banan understands the material but the way she structures her notes is not very engaging and not the most helpful, since they are mostly fill-in-the-blank which can be boring. The practice exams that she gives are nothing like the actual exams, which are much more difficult.

Lectures are so random, like you'll be sitting there taking notes, and then the topic will change. You'll get really confused because it makes no sense how she organizes notes. Lecture is also so boring that you'll lose focus then literally nothing will make sense. Don't let the past ratings fool you, the exams and practice exams are nothing alike.

I'm not a huge fan of Banan. She's one of those professors who's VERY bothered by people talking in class and frequently stops mid-lecture to shush people, which is really annoying. Her practice exams are not like her actual exams. I am an engineer on the Dean's List, and this is genuinely one of my hardest classes. A LOT of content is covered.
The actual tests are significantly harder than the practice exams. It's nothing alike. She does explain the slides in lecture, but it goes so fast because theres so much material to be covered.

Lectures were disorganized and hard to follow, making simple concepts confusing. Fill-in-the-blank slides and long explanations didn't help with understanding. I had to rely on outside resources to learn the material. She would talk about stories that had zero correlation to the topics. The issue wasn't the subject, but how poorly it was taught.

analysis.name: David Blon
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Blon is an incredibly thoughtful director. When I came to Purdue, everyone told me I would not like him, but he has proved that wrong. He cares about the individual lives of his students in a very admirable way, and he wants to get to know each one personally. He is absolutely the director that makes me feel the most at home in Purdue Bands.

Dr. Blon is a controversial figure in the department. He can be a bit more picky than the average director, but all things considered, he really cares about his students and wants them to be them to be the best they possibly can be. If you plan on skipping class or not putting in 100% effort (no judgement here), switch to a different professor.

Every band director leads rehearsals and performances in their own way and has preference of repertoire, and Dr. Blon clearly cares about each performer in his ensemble and each instrument. In addition he cares about fundamentals like tuning and attention to detail. I think some of the reviews here are unfair or just inaccurate.

He was super chill during class and picked out good music. He wants you to be there but doesn't make a huge deal about absences/lateness. Not sure what band y'all have been in that plays through pieces completely before stopping for feedback? Overall, chill prof, less strict than my high school director. Not sure what other reviews are talking abt

Was disappointed in the inaccuracies of other ratings. He is not biased against anyone. He is a great man who truly cares. Directors have lives of their own, some have a harder time hiding the effects of their personal lives and state of the world on their mood than others, but this does not make him a bad director/person, he is one of the best.

analysis.name: Osman Basaran
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Basaran knows what he's talking about, but you never will. He moves quickly through material, gives WAY too much homework, and the exams are impossible. But hang in there, apparently everyone gets a B in the end.

Amazing that time cannot dull his issues. Obviously brilliant man, but no real connection with the students or understanding of what he is (or in most cases, is NOT) clearly conveying. Very obvious from his test averages- in my class 13%, 21%, 24% and a whopping 30% on the final exam.  Its Purdue, you do have a choice in professors.  Chose wisely!

Learned more in this class than in all my other ChE courses I took in the last year.  You have to be ready to learn fast and keep on top of your toes otherwise you'll start falling behind before the second week of class.  He assumes you know everything from physics and calculus.  If you're stuck on concepts he'll gladly help you at office hours.

Professor Basaran was a great professor who really made the course content interesting and delivered great lectures. However, the homeworks and exams were extremely difficult with very low average scores. Overall great professor who made the class interesting and was always willing to help, but the content of the course was very difficult.

Dr. Basaran is an inspirational professor. His passion toward his subject is infectious and motivates you to pursue research in fluid mechanics! The subject material he covers finds direct use in understanding many aspects of research in diverse fields. He is tough but fair. I wholeheartedly recommend taking any courses he teaches, totally worth it

analysis.name: Michael Brownstein
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Brownstein was super condescending the entire semester. He is incredibly arrogant and mean towards his students and looks to call people out in front of the whole lecture. Guy makes his quizzes and tests 10x more complicated and difficult than it needs to be. Tries to act smart, but is an airhead. The TA was an absolute moron as well. Avoid him.

Avoid. Creates such a tense learning enviornment and is always looking to call out students for not paying attention. Has no personality whatsoever and lectures feel like an interrogation. Quizzes are graded harshly and the averages are always in the 60s. Told the class “your quiz grades are bad so pay attention. Arrogant and overbearing

Y'all know the scene in Interstellar (2014) where Cooper is trying to get his past self not to leave Murph? That's how I feel about my past self choosing to take this class with Prof. Brownstein. The man will fail you even if you follow his instructions perfectly. Complaints about clarity, but he will not give you enough time to clarify anything.

Everything a professor should strive NOT to be. Super condescending and scornful, always looking to call out students for the most minor things. Quiz and exam questions consist of minor facts he briefly mentions in lecture that do not relate to key course objectives. Super rude, and does not have a personality. Embarrassment to Purdue honestly.

AVOID AVOID AVOID. He was extremely condescending and quite frankly just mean to students in class, claiming they were doing things they definitely weren't (talking/cheating) and being more of a distraction himself than the students causing issues. The quizzes/tests most of the time felt like it was over things we didn't even discuss. Just no.

analysis.name: Brian Zuel
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He's an AI Bro. He loves LLMs and will find a way to shove them into every lecture and every assignment. Instead of teaching us how a powershell script that he used for an in class demo worked he instead taught us his Claude prompt wrote to generate the script. I am convinced that he's forgotten every piece of knowledge he ever learned in college

He just reads off his slides and does not go into detail much. He has many ALAS. There have been occasions which he assigns them and does not tell the class which unless we look, we would have no clue. The lab assignments are hard and are not very in-depth with how their manuals are written and doesn't much instruction.

No attendance mandatory, does a lot of ALAS but they are fun to do. Will never regrade. His TA, Shetty, is the worst try to avoid him at all costs. He will never reply to emails and will not help you in labs. Tough grader and will not give you clear feedback even in person. The professor is always on the TA side. Just stay away from this TA.

attendance not required but some activities missed if you don't come. LABS R SO MUCH WORK. they have strict guidelines and are confusing. manuals and rubrics don't align. you spend hours trouble shooting to only get 50% on labs because it didn't work for you. Overall if you put your blood, sweat, and tears you can get the A. Exams are online.

Zuel was a pretty good lecturer and pretty chill. Would never lecture for the entire 50 minutes. The labs at first were kind of hard to get through, but they got easier as the semester went along and were actually kind of fun. There is a ton of extra credit too.

analysis.name: Brian  Metzger
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lecture goes fast. Pay attention to both what he says and writes. Homework is tricky (Weekly ~25 problems upwards of 70 total parts). There is supplemental reading but isn't "required". Exam was VERY computationally heavy (similar to the homework), but the multiple choice nature of it makes it relatively nicer. 1 crib sheet allowed on the exam.

This is the worst professor in my life. He with strong accent speaks so fast, it's impossible to understand. Once a weekly assignment had nearly 100 questions. At exam, I almost laughed, if you were to actually compute the calculation problems step by step, it would take 40+ minutes, as if deriving everything from ancient times to the AI era.
spiritual cell-level hypnotist.
If you are forced to take it, I'm sorry. If not, RUN!!!

analysis.name: Samuel Bennett
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor is very intense. He is extremely focused on perceived behavior in his class, and he will berate someone publicly if he thinks they are not paying attention, or if they leave their book at home. He creates a tense environment for all students. He grades fairly but is intense with comments, many of which are mean-spirited and destructive.

Change proffessors. There is too much work in this class for no readon whatsoever. There are many other scla proffessors that will not give you this much work to do. SCLA should not be that much work. He is a very tough grader. He is a good person person though.

He has his own interpretations of the books being read, and says he values “pushback” and “alternative viewpoints”, but then instead of supporting forming your own views, he tries to disprove them to make his point “correct”. 

This makes people not want to even consider having their own thoughts, which is the whole purpose of being a teacher

Prof. Bennett was a very engaging professor to take class with. He was open to all sorts of ideas no matter how absurd they were. I will admit, if you're taking SCLA101 for the credit and only care about grades, this prof is not for you. However, if you're willing to put in that extra work to read and analyze, his class is very rewarding.

Professor Bennett, unlike most professors at Purdue, has a great personality and shows a keen interest towards teaching his classes. If you come with the mentality of wanting to learn, you would enjoy this class very much. The lectures, too, are fun as the professor brings in a positive energy everyday. Great guy!

analysis.name: Cecilia Ying
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This professor is honestly so bad at teaching and the lectures are completely different from the recitations. The TAs don't know anything about what they're teaching and we're blindly expected to know what to do on the labs. The midterm was bad as well as the professor didn't even talk about 1/3 of the contents on it n now my GPA is suffering.

The lectures have almost nothing to do with the recitations. Lab grades didn't come out for 3 weeks, while we had already submitted another one. Doing iClicker in lecture, 80% of people were getting the questions wrong because they didn't know what she was talking about. I dropped bc I'm CODO'ing to HK & this class was a complete waste of my time.

Wished our demo was longer and less rushed. It was a fun project to build our own chatbot regardless. Second half of the course was way easier with less technical stuff and more business applications. Professor tries to make the class interesting by including games and in class discussions. It's a good intro class.

Great class to tie technical fundamentals to business principles, going beyond just learning how to use AI but elements that helps companies to be successful in their AI implementations. Professor is also passionate about teaching and incorporating so many in class activities to keep things interesting. Great class!

She really tries to make the lectures interesting and fun by including games. She also talks about how the labs connect to the concepts we learned in each lecture - clearly some people who don't come to class won't know what's going on. It's a tough class, but you will also learned a lot. Take it!

analysis.name: Chuck Krousgrill
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: One of the best teachers I have ever had!

If you have the chance to take a class with Prof. Krousgrill, DO IT! I was lucky to have him for ME274 & for ME323, and he is a great teacher. His lecture book is a must-buy and if you show up to class (he does random quizzes but not often) often times you only have to write your name to get credit. His content matches exams, which is appreciated.
I'm currently taking ME 200 under Sojka and ME 274 under Krousgrill. I skip 50% of my ME 200 lectures and attended 100% of his lectures. That just shows how interesting his class is.
Very caring good professor, if you are taking ME274 or 323, take it with Krous!
Krousgrill is a great professor. He teaches at a somewhat slower pace in my opinion, which worked well for me. I had him for ME 274 and ME 323, and I really enjoyed him.

analysis.name: Clyde Sorell
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: You spend a lot of time preparing many presentations. Never choose him

The request is really really hard to satisfy. He even graded me low for the reason that my slides' style is not unitive. He said the different slide was in different style and give me a really low grade.
Although the professor has many different tasks, as long as you work hard, you can get high marks!!

analysis.name: Clark Cory
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This is for CM360. Clark is extremely disrespectful, and will send very unprofessional and unclear emails. One of his emails has read “nope try again” in response to a very lengthy emails asking questions. This is especially unforgiving due to the fact that this class is only in person one day of the week. He also does not use bright space. 0/10

I never thought I'd ever find a class with such a workload for 2 credits. Clark is great outside of class. very understanding when it comes to health and personal matters outside of the classroom. But in class, its like a flip switches. If you don't understand it the first time, good luck... and be ready to spend a lot of hours on AutoCAD.

Great professor that obviously knew what he was talking about. Lectures were very important despite not being mandatory. The time spent on homework every week was more than all of my other classes combined but definitely worth it. Midterm is tough and definitely do not put off the final project!

Professor Cory is a professor that clearly cares about his students. The homework assignments are lengthy, usually taking 3+ hours per assignment, but he works through many of the assignments in lecture. Don't put off any projects, especially the final project which easily takes 50+ hours to complete.

He's argumentative and narrow-minded. He doesn't help/review coursework out before tests/midterms. Before our final he told us we weren't allowed to ask him or any of our TA's questions to help us prepare.

analysis.name: Jan Cover
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Cover is one of the best! He is so kind! He definitely has a persona, but if you get to know him you'll realize how helpful and nice he is. He actually cares about his students which is rare to find nowadays. Is the class challenging, yes? You have to have a real interest in philosophy to enjoy this course. He is a great professor!!!

If you take a class with him, be careful when you speak in class. If you're expecting to be able to disagree with something he says without him yelling at you/claiming you're stupid, you'll be in for a shock. On the one hand, he is a good professor in that he makes you think, but on the other hand, it's always his way or the highway.

Cover is the rudest most out-of-pocket professor I've ever had. Not sure why a ton of dudes seem to idolize him and excuse his poor behavior by referencing how good of a philosopher he is. Despite what he says he does NOT care about his students, or how well they do in the class. It's boring and you won't get anything important out of it.

While he often goes on tirades completely unrelated to philosophy and berates the students, he cares about his students and teaches important concepts well. Don't take this class if you want an easy A. Make sure to do your readings, try your hardest, and go to class and you will succeed in his classes.

Cover teaches unlike any other professor at Purdue. Be prepared to think in a way none of your other classes have taught you to think. His teaching style may brush people's feathers but overall the content he teaches is valuable.

analysis.name: Charles Catalano
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Charlie is by far the best teacher I have ever had. Not only does he make an english SPEAKING class fun, but the books he chose for us, the assignments, the videos we watch in class, and his whole demeanor is just so inspirational and interesting and it feels like you're truly learning for the first time. He is someone you will never forget.

This is the first time ive really cared about an english/lit class in a long time. Charlie is inspirational and really cares about his students not only in his class, but going forward. Hes the type that will say hi if he sees you 2 years after you had him. Im bad at public speech, but hes a forgiving grader and gave me Bs on all my speeches.

It is clear how much Charlie not only loves his job, but loves other people. He showed genuine care for his students and clearly wanted everyone to succeed. My favorite moment was the line of students after our last lecture lining up to give him a hug, or just thank him. If you have to take SCLA102, take it with Charlie.
Charlie is an incredible professor with genuine passion not just for what he teaches but for life in general

Professor Charlie has been the most passionate professor I have had at Purdue so far. It is clear that he cares about his work and the impact on students. He does a great job of bringing the real world into the classroom for deeper learning.

analysis.name: Joseph (Kuan-Hua) Chen
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 181 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Holy cow Dr. Chen is great. Actually had a different professor for Calc 3 and I skipped all of his lectures so I could watch Chen's lectures online. Great handwriting, explains things at a reasonable level and pace. Gave me an unreasonable standard to hold the rest of my professors to.

Prof Chen IS the Purdue Math department, despite having different professors along the way this man has carried me from MA 162 to MA 303 with his recorded lectures. His explanations and lectures are incredibly thorough and he explains in a way that resonates with many students. His exams can sometimes be tough, but are fair. Thank you Prof Chen!

Chenflix saved my life during math courses at purdue (162, 261, 266), and I've heard his in person lectures are even better. Very good at breaking topics down, explaining how to do them, and why we do them. Very efficient teaching style with not a lot of time being wasted too. analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Highly request all of you to not take his MGMT 382 class.I have suffered immensely in this class. All other 382 sections have such an easy exam and project, most of my other friends got through it with an easy A, but my grades fell and how. Not organized at all, very difficult exams, no curve scale, and everything is wrong about it.

This is my favorite professor I have had at Purdue! I don't even like econ, and am not good at it. I just needed to take this course. He truly cares about his students and gives so many opportunities to earn points. I remember him bringing donuts & starbucks. His kids passed out our exams. He is so caring and funny and an amazing professor!
There was no reason to have closed-book exams, too many concepts, examples, models... you need to remember everything for the exam! There was no way a student can meet his requirement for exam.

Hands down one of the best professors I've ever had. Really cares about your learning and makes every effort from his side to make sure you're doing okay. I've never asked him for help and not got my problem resolved, whether academic or logistical.

Easily one of my favorite professors I have had while at Purdue! He is always willing to meet outside of office hours and if a very interesting lecture ( I actually wanted to go to his class and I do not even like Econ)!

analysis.name: Mark Lehto
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lectures consist of Prof. Lehto basically standing at the front of the room having a conversation with himself about very general topics called out in his slides. Doesn't go into much detail and does not give a good idea of specific information that students need to know. To prepare for exams you just need to read every line of the textbook.
Worst professor so far. Cant hear him in the class, no past exams and practices provided, exams are hard especially for international students.

The professor is extremely confusing in his incoherent ramblings. The material itself is quite interesting. The lecture material is presented much differently than in the book. The tests are much more detailed and difficult than the class ever prepares you for. All-in-all, probably the most miserable class I have ever taken. Tests are curved.

Tests contain material that was never covered. HW & tests are never reviewed. Graded work does not contain corrections or information to help you learn. Never does problems in class. Provides no help via email. TA's provide no help. 893 pages assigned reading (a statistics class). Text and reading's 50+ years old. No online office hours.

Very disorganized class. There is a thousand things you get graded on and every single one of them is all over the place. Lectures themselves are ungoable because they are so boring and do not even matter for the exam. The exam is just a random stuff that could have been talked about in the past two months. No study guide or example exam whatsoever

analysis.name: Tongseok Lim
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I don't know why his rating his so low. Perhaps that was for a different course. In my opinion, one of the best, most hardworking and caring professors I've ever had. I truly appreciate like the way he explains stuff which made difficult concepts easier to grasp. Would definitely take again and recommend (at least certainly for this course).
Breaks down the concepts well and provide supplemental videos

Can confirm that he does not know anything he is talking about. He reads off of the textbook for simple concepts, shows YouTube videos when he's too lazy to explain core concepts, or just doesn't understand it himself. Use excuses like "rubrics limit the learning potential" for not having ANY clear instructions on what the final project should be.

The class content is fairly easy and has a lot in common with statistics and basic machine learning. The professor is the worst. He doesn't know what he is teaching and uses YouTube videos to do half of the lecture. The entire course is poorly organized and the grading rubric is unclear. Definitely not recommended.

The content in this course can be dry and difficult to learn, but Dr. Lim does his best to give effective lectures. He is very nice and is great at lecturing. The course is hybrid and grading is mostly attendance, homework, and projects.

analysis.name: Ming-Yu  Ngai
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Ming acts caring in class, but destroys you on every exam then proceeds to gaslight you to show up to lecture and office hours. Could use more Christian values when writing exams. The TAs convince you that you don't belong studying chemistry, and refuse to help or explain material. If you're a chemistry major, life gets better after this class.

The (rare) times we go over easy topics he slows down but any other material that is difficult is incredibly sped up to the point where you need outside resources to understand any of the things going on. You can have full understanding of lecture topics, homework, lab, etc. and still get a bad grade because the exams are made so difficult.

Does not care/humiliates students asking questions. Exam 2 average was 44% and students received same advice from exam 1. Head TA writes exams difficult on purpose which other graduate TAs disapprove of. No curve provided. Rushes through content in lecture, does not answer questions. Academic advisors had to audit course after students complained.

Bro truly couldn't give a gaf about you. He has failing exam averages and he just says that YOU could be doing more to do well rather than reevaluating his own teaching methods. He should not be teaching an orgo class designed for CHEM MAJORS if a good chunk of people are currently failing.

Extremely Rude to students, Rushes through lecture, clearly does not care about students nor their mental wellbeing. Class averaged a score of lower 60s for an exam to which Ngai responded "I don't understand, this is easy you should've gotten higher than this"

analysis.name: Kenji Matsuki
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 281 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: He is very thorough in his lectures. He goes over sample problems for the homework every class and gives worked-out solutions to the study guide. As long as you go over the study guide you should get a C in the class. Kenji constantly goes, "Are you okay?" or when the class is confused he says, "Oh no, I am failing" and explains the concept again.

Purdue math is notoriously difficult, but having Kenji as your professor helps a lot. He is entertaining and it is easy to pay attention to his lectures. His study guides are essential for the exams, but be prepared for the exam average to be around a 65 no matter how hard you study. If there's a way for you to have Kenji for Calc 1 or 2, do it!

This dude has some good lectures and study guides, but he has flipped me off almost every day. No professor has ever done that to me but this guy does it almost everyday. Goated and hilarious prof tho. Must take if you get the chance. 
I could also say that besides the study guide solve the past exams and boiler exams as well. Just dont tell him.
Remember, when the graph of ln(x) approaches zero, in goes D E E P D O W N.

Kenji is one of the best math professors. If you have the option between MA 161/162 and MA 165/166, ALWAYS choose 165/166. Matsuki has fun lectures and an extremely useful study guide that is very similiar to the test. My only critique is that sometimes he will take longer than promised to release the answer key to that study guide. Great professor

analysis.name: Ning Zhou
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The accent for non-Chinese speakers takes time to adjust but the content delivered is clear. Her pacing during lectures is good and reserves time to answer many questions asked by students. Professor Zhou is all business, no play, so the lectures will require high concentration. She also cares about her students and hopes they succeed.

Her lectures are not helpful. Long lecture quizzes (20–30 minutes) leave little time to learn new concepts. She doesn't explain code clearly and often can't answer questions due to the next class. Learning relies on TAs and self-study. The workload is manageable, but if you want to learn during lectures, I don't recommend taking her.

Lectures are dry. The packet's practice tests are essential for the grade. Don't buy the textbook; it's rarely used. Rigid classroom: assigned seating and no talking. Communication via email and in-class questions is difficult. Quizzes run long. Coordinate with your Lab TA for help.

Professor Zhou genuinely cares about her students and puts a lot of effort into teaching. CS159 is hard, but she explains concepts clearly and makes it easier to understand. Office hours are very helpful, and the lecture quizzes after each topic really help reinforce the material
Her lectures are very dry and boring but she seems to genuinely care about the class doing good. This class is pretty easy if you have prior programming experience so lecture isn't that important

analysis.name: Najmus Saqib
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of the best Professors. Lectures are clear and concise, recommend printing lecture notes prior to class. Balanced homework, reinforces what you learned without being obnoxiously difficult or long. Exams are reasonable length and difficulty, Does really good reviews and is clear what is on the exams. Class act professor.

The lecture notes are informative, detailed, and easy to follow. He explains common mistakes and why they're wrong, making concepts simple to grasp. Attending his office hours will help you 100% ace the class. He genuinely helps you succeed. He makes learning fun, connects with students, and his passion for explaining the concepts shows up!
I really enjoyed Professor Saqib teaching. Course was well organized and he clearly cares about the students learning
Top 1 professor oat. Genuinely feels like he cares about every student and it is clear to me that he is passionate about what he does.
takes time to know student, great lecturer!

analysis.name: Philip Mummert
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 100 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: If Isaac Newton and God had a baby, it would be this man. Because of him, math is never about rote memorization but pure, intuitive internalization. Literally a one in a billion talent. I would name all my kids after him. My GPA is saved, my soul is ascended. We are truly not worthy. The absolute goat. 11/10.

He's the goat. Amazing lectures, witty, very knowledgeable about more than just math, like lowk calc3 lectures were often the highlight of the day. The class is a good heat check if u think ur smart. If u really are you'll do great, if u don't it's cuz ur not - no excuses/blaming the professor, and tests are very fair. Truly enjoyable and rewarding

Professor Mummert was an amazing calc 3 lecturer. Textbook is required to access the homework but you do not need to read it because his lectures are so good. He always makes sure to cover what will be on the homework and the exams. He also makes very good analogies to calc 1 and clearly knows his stuff. You definitely need to study for quizzes.

Dr. Mummert has a uniform lecture style. He reviews a problem from the previous topic, explains the intuition of the new topic, and then gives a formal definition that we use to solve examples until the class ends. He is caring and invested during office hours. I have no complaints other than he forgets that nothing is trivial to underclassmen.

Dr. Mummert was the first professor I met in college. He gave me the best first impression of Purdue, and he really knows his stuff. My single gripe is that I noticed he tends to have difficulty understanding a student's query if they're not 100% precise. Super funny dude, literally friends with him to this day.

analysis.name: Dominic Naughton
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 100 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: If you tried to design the perfect math professor, you would wind up with someone like Dr. Naughton. Super clear lectures, steady pace, boilercast, easy to approach, and on top of that he's hilarious too. You'll never walk out of lecture confused (something very rare in Purdue math!)

Best MA162 prof, other than Peter Cook possibly. Very clear. Moves fast in lecture, so write fast! Seemed like a cool and nice guy. Always listened to students' opinions/ideas on how to attack problems differently. Very knowledgeable. A+
Very solid teacher! Lectures are a little boring, but thats more about the material than anything! Notes go along good with homework but not so much for the quizzes or exams.
Great lectures. Clearly explains things, and allows for things to be reexplained if needed. Highly recommend.

He is a really great professor that teaches Calculus so that everyone in his class will understand it. He's very clear and organized and always willing to help! He's also Irish, so his voice is great to listen to.

analysis.name: Seunghoon Na
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Must attend his lectures as his lecture notes complement the lectures. Very passionate about the subject and brilliant if you show enthusiasm in class. Had very engaging ideas on economic growth and always open to me discussing the topic beyond what the course might cover. Deepended my understanding of growth economics as a whole.

Horrible...Regrets not having listened to others' advice not to take his class. Boring class, strong accent, not a lot of real-world experience. Lectures are conceptual while homework and exams are mathematical. The only good thing is that the exam is very similar to homework. But even if I memorized all the homework problems for the exam, only 75%

This is the least I've ever understood a class. His lectures are so hard to understand, and irrelevant to the actual concepts- I'd say that only around 15 minutes of every lecture actually teaches you how to complete the problems. He is also not receptive to questions, so there is no actual way to learn in this class outside of teaching yourself.

He is literally the worst at teaching! His lesson plans have no flow and you can barely understand what he is saying. He randomly uses Calculus 2 in the course even though its not a pre-req for the class.

We didn't learn much of anything about economics in this class. Everything in lecture was completely theoretical, while the tests and quizzes were all quantitative problems that we had never seen before. Once spent an entire class talking about a model only for him to say it doesn't work. Useless class and bad instruction.

analysis.name: Jennifer Nelson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: A harsh person. Class is easy but she doesn't really want to give the tough student an A. She just try to find some small error then she can curve your grade down. Make you feel confused and disappointed, you only have a little step behind A, but finally you can't touch it.

It feels unreasonable to have in-person exams covering so much material, especially the third midterm. It's surreal that professors expect this level of commitment for a 100-level Gen Ed course. My friend who took it last semester had a much easier experience

She is definitely a good teacher, the grading criteria is so clear and keeps tracking your progress.
The lectures are mandatory for credits. The labs are long but easy to get a high grade.
The exams cover too much material sometimes, but she keeps the average above 80. And she is open to drop the lowest score, which is definitely good news.

Really unnecessarily difficult. Take literally any other eaps 100-level course. There's hours of lecture and readings every week and the homework is unnecessarily time consuming for what the class is. It's really not bad, but compared to the other intro eaps classes it is ridiculous.

Understands this is a mandatory class for college of science, doesn't make lectures needlessly difficult. Lenient with grading however the projects are a lot more work than I feel they should be. Not bad for a great issues in science class all in all.

analysis.name: Sam Nariman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is a brilliant instructor who is not afraid to keep things light in the classroom which helps with how heavy the course material is. Extremely low test averages but generous curves. He is a great professor outside the classroom and encouraged me to broaden my horizons when thinking about Mathematics as a whole. Loved interacting with him.

Easily the hardest class I've ever taken. Professor is clearly knowledgeable on the subject and cares about his students. His lectures are good and if you can follow along he does well to explain what is otherwise very dense and esoteric. Book is difficult to follow for the mathematically immature and exams are very hard. Don't expect a good grade.

Very poorly organized course. No slides or online materials and no clear study guides prior to exams. Study guides are just reading the entire textbook (300 pages) and test questions are hard and cover very specific parts of the book (not general topics). Also lectures are mostly just him writing very illegibly on chalkboard and he grades strict.

Functions like a typical upper-level math course. Prof expects you to have a ton of general intuition whilst the only supplementary material is a very terse textbook. Final exam was not even cummulative and unless you had somehow memorized proofs, you were going to fail. The TA was brilliant, would have passed the course if he was teaching it.

Explains concepts very intuitively and follows the book very closely, so if you miss a lecture it's really easy to get caught up. Also, his class is interactive and he builds on concepts slowly and carefully, making sure everything is clear at he does. I'd definitely take him again for this class. Also, his exams aren't very difficult (IMO).

analysis.name: Oleksandr Tsymbaliuk
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Quite possibly the greatest professor I've ever had at this school. One of the best lecturers I've ever come across. Make no mistake though, this is a brutally difficult course. The content is manageable, but the pace is extremely quick and the exams are quite difficult. Well worth it (IMO), I've learned so much in such a short amount of time.

Awesome guy, impeccable lecture notes. Really caring in office hours. Has a strong accent but still understandable. Manageable homework loads. However, exams are really difficult (maybe complex analysis is just difficult in general). Skippable final which is a big plus. Honestly on the better end of math professors at Purdue.

Some of the best math lectures I have experienced at this school. He explains content at a good pace, simplifies definitions when necessary, takes questions, and gives warm-up and in-class problems. He is also very open during office hours and will take time to explain anything one-on-one.
I felt unprepared for exams too.

Probably the best professor I've ever had. He is a lovely, happy, and upbeat guy who is very good at explaining and connecting concepts. In the past I've been more fond of computational math classes but he made me find a passion for theory based math. If you have the chance, take his class.

analysis.name: Valerie O'Brien
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. O'Brien was the BEST professor that I have had during my time so far at Purdue. Her lectures cover a lot of content in a short period of time, but she makes it clear when concepts mentioned will be on exams, letting you know exactly what to study. She is very knowledgeable and it is clear that she genuinely cares about her students' learning.

Probably the best pre-pharmacy professor here. She teaches immunology with ease and explicitly states when concepts being taught will be mentioned on exams. She's also so enjoyable to listen to, and there are multiple lectures where she has everyone laughing. Loved Dr. O'Brien downnn, wish she taught the entire class and not just half of it :(

Great lecturer, probably the best in BSPS or pre-pharm. Assignments helpful for studying if you put in effort and don't use AI, and she creates tests that are based entirely off lectures. It is a hard class, but possible to get an A/B if you follow along. Lectures are fine to watch on your own, but don't get behind because it's a lot of content.

She is a very concise lecturer and makes difficult concepts easier to understand. The tests are based directly on the lecture. It's definitely possible to get an A if you memorize the lectures and pay attention in class.

analysis.name: Jun Oh
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I was worried with the bad reviews, but most of the content was not hard to follow. Guessing that most of the reviews are from an earlier period. The exams were difficult, but we were told what to study. This course was more difficult than most but not the hardest I have ever taken.
Disagree with the previous rating. Professor Oh no has no prior experience and makes the exams unnecessarily hard.
He knows what he is talking about. Concepts are pretty clear. Although I would say that the class is challenging
Disagree with the previous rating. Professor Oh has prior experience and makes reasonable exams

analysis.name: Samuel O'Connor
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Sam O'Connor is not the course coordinator for this class, so I want to give him a bit of grace. I found theclass quite easy, and I think that's because his lectures were pretty solid. The only bad thing is that I found it hard to connect with him, and he speaks very quietly. Sit up front for this class.

Grades are really just the exams and quizzes so was hard to bring my grade up after a tough start. Class is taught at a quick pace and not very in depth or time for in class help. Boiler exam is the most helpful thing to prepare for exams and finals.

I was in this guys class for one week and his lectures were terrible. He talks so light and his hand is blocking the screen the whole time which just leaves you writing so fast and not understanding the whole time. He also has no note outlines, looking back on notes is just hard. His quizzes are significantly harder than the other professors too.

analysis.name: Temitope   Olenloa
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: All of the concerns raised in previous reviews are accurate and align with my experience in this course. The class felt consistently disorganized, with unclear structure and expectations throughout the semester. Instructions for assignments were often ambiguous, which made it difficult to understand what was required. Stay away from Dr. Temi.

Professor Olenloa is extremely disorganized and consistently fails to provide clear or coherent instructions for assignments, making expectations difficult to understand. Feedback is vague and unhelpful, offering little to no guidance on what was done correctly or how to improve, which significantly undermines the learning experience.

Overall, not the worst Honors First Year Experience Professor, she was just disorganized and the rubrics were a bit vague. Not hard, but would advise choosing a different professor. She teaches Student Motivation, which may be helpful to some but wasn't to me personally. She was really kind, however, and was passionate about her area of expertise.

I've never seen such a disorganized professor in my entire life. You will be snowed under with unnecessary and unclear work and spend hours on daily basis for assignments that seem like they are made up just to fill the syllabus. She is extremely tough grader and her feedback is highly ambiguous.

Dr. Temi's class tends to be disorganized and often confusing. Content can be hard to find, expectations are unclear. She messed up grades for multiple students in my class. She grades very easily on the assignments only to be harsh on the final. Grades sometimes don't make sense. I felt like I left the class frustrated and learning little.

analysis.name: Orla Hart
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very unorganized. Was late on posting the exams and assignments. She is a nice person, not a great teacher. She talks like she is on 2x speed and does not have the best lecture slides. There was a lot of info on the exams that were never talked about in class. The exams are extremely wording and give you no time to process the question.

Dr. Hart was my favorite professor this semester. While her lectures were not mandatory, they were always fun and interesting. Lectures were mostly helpful for case study sessions, as Dr. Hart and the TAs were available to help. She is often difficult to reach over email, but if you ask a question in person or follow-up, she is very willing to help

Definitely a good professor, but I think the class is challenging. The advice I would give is to read the textbook and know the content before coming to class, and be engaged. Incrementally studying will ensure that studying for the exams is not a chore. Exams are not a joke and are synthesis-based with some route memorization.

Professor Hart is a wonderful woman and very passionate about biochemistry. Unfortunately, her exams were extremely difficult. I did not fail this class only because she gave a good amount of extra credit towards the end of the semester. The exams were long and in paragraphs and you are given less than a minute for each question to read and answer.

Dr. Hart breezes through lectures, so do readings before class!! The exams had recommended time limits on the questions and did not let you go back which made them tricky. Even if you knew the content the real-world applications made it difficult to prepare for. Overall OK class, just wish she slowed down and elaborated on important things.

analysis.name: Jacob  Ott
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Ott did an amazing job of explaining concepts that were boring or challenging. He offers optional homework problems that align very close with exam material. He also posts practice exams that are super similar to the format of the mid terms. If you go to class, ask questions, and participate you should have no problems succeeding.

The material for this course is difficult and boring; I did not enjoy taking it in the early morning. However, the proffesor is great at explaining each topic, caring and effective at answering questions. I did feel surprised on any exams. Overall, great instructor, but you signed up for accounting, so be prepared to feel eepy.

Only exams and quizzes are graded. Material is not easy nor hard to understand, you have to go to lectures, pay attention in class, and do the homework to do well. If you do those things, it'll be hard to get anything less than a B, since each exam is curved. Ott is good at what he does, he knows the material and can answer questions well.

If you do not have much prior accounting knowledge, this class may be challenging. The course is worth 400 points, with exams making up the majority of the grade, so exam performance is HIGHLY important. Quizzes are straightforward, and staying on top of the material is essential.

Professor Ott is one of the best professors I have had here in my time at Purdue. His lectures are the most useful out of any class I take currently. Exams can be challenging but there is a curve and he provides a coupious amount of practice problems.

analysis.name: Yulia Pushkar
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If I could name a worse professor in Purdue, this professor Yulia Pushkar would be one. She is unprepared, unprofessional and a disgrace to the teaching community. This class was an absolute waste of my time and all graduate students in that class. I advise that she stops teaching and enroll in an institution where she can seek mental help.

This was a poorly prepared class. Prof. Yulia Pushkar did not prepare her lectures ahead of time, she was insulting to students who asked questions when she was not being clear.This professor is offensive and inadequate. I do not recommend taking any class with her.
This professor should not be allowed to teach! Its shocking how she got into teaching!Please go back to doing another profession.

Unclear, not helpful and overall does not seem like even she has a full grasp of the concepts. You are better off reading the book and looking up youtube videos than attending lectures. Grading is inconsistent and does not give a good representation of how much a student knows.
One suggestion, run away. Worst class I've taken in my life. Get ready to read the textbook. Lectures are useless, but have to attend for iClickers. I don't think it can get worse

analysis.name: Paul Thomas
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor definitely has an ego problem and it is the most busy work class I've ever taken. He caps getting an A at 93 and above, which is incredibly selfish. There's no reason I should have more work in this class than CNIT 470. Take this class online over the summer if you can and get ready for a repeat of CNIT 182.

The professor decided to change the grading scale for this course this past semester, so you only get an A if you have a 94 and above which is NOT ideal. It is an easy class if you do the work and the reading and the concepts are explained well in lab and in lecture. TAs will grade project harshly so just make corrections and be thorough with that.

Paul Thomas is very rude and passive aggressive. His grading scale is completely ridiculous (a A starts at a 93) and it just never really felt like he wanted to teach or be there at all. Labs depend heavily on your TA but aren't too bad. Study hard for tests, and the group project only sucks if your group sucks.

Paul Thomas is a good professor, he is very fair in his grading and has set the class up so that if you do bad in one category you can make it up in others. He knows what he is talking about and lectures are clear enough, and he likes answering questions if you do have them. Very respectable dude.

Paul is too funny. One day he would get angry at someone for asking a question and then the next day he starts singing in the middle of class. Genuinely a decent lecturer but he is too passive aggressive.

analysis.name: Vaibhav Pandey
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Easily the best math professor I've had at Purdue. Takes the time to explain topics and does lots of examples to help you understand the content. Comprehensive review before exams that prepare you well. Always responds to emails and has office hours to help when needed, and doesn't shame you for it. TAKE MATH WITH PANDEY!!!

Professor Pandey is a great, thoughtful lecturer. He wrote everything out alongside us so tempo was not too rushed. Every class began with definitions and content, then 2-4 practice problems that he went over. There was never a concept on HW or exams that Pandey did not cover clearly. No attendance required, but go to his class!

One of the best Purdue math professors. He is super clear in everything he says, and explains everything extremely thoroughly, even going into simple proofs of the concepts that we are learning. Exams are fair, and he takes feedback from the students after each one as well, and adjusts accordingly, however questions' weights could be adjusted.

Prof. Pandey a great math professor. Explains concepts very well and also encourages discussion about problems in lecture and participation.
His homework and tests are pretty fair. Only thing I wish was different is that MCQs/True-False questions are worth too many points.
Otherwise, great prof. Take his class if you can.

really good professor. teaches slowly and clearly. his exams kinda annoyed me because the short answer/mult choice were 10 pts each out of 100 so if u get 2 mult choice wrong ur alr down to a B-. no extra credit. hes prob one of the best profs ive had here tho he teaches rly well, i just wasnt v good at it.

analysis.name: Tiantian Qin
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

Before coming into this class i had a working knowledge of statistics. After leaving i can honestly say i have no idea what i am doing. Professor Qin does a poor job of wording her thoughts, has no organization in her lecture, and moves insanely fast through difficult subject matter. When asked to clarify she often confuses the entire class more.

She seems to be motivated, but she makes her students feel desperate. The biggest problem is that she skipped many procedures required for the student to study for review or preview. Another problem is that her midterm is too difficult to solve in time. If solving the questions had been worthwhile, I would have not felt frustrated.

Do not take this course.  I spend 10+ hours per week on the homework.  The online book is difficult to navigate and doesn't align well with the class powerpoints.  The instructor moves way too quickly.   Worst course I've taken at Purdue.

This professor is knowledgeable in statistics, but could not be worse at teaching the material in a manor that is accessible or understandable. The majority of time in class is spent in confusion. If you want to bond with other students over just how confused you are, this is the class for you!

analysis.name: Qiang Liu

Final exam also covered many things that weren't mentioned in class and was extremely difficult. Prof also laughs at students for getting answers wrong.
Professor Liu is a very easygoing professor, and always makes class interesting :)
Very smart professor, great lectures
Great guy. He really cares about the students and the subject matter. Easily one of the most applicable courses (and projects) that I've had at Purdue. He does take attendance though.
terrible professor. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS.

analysis.name: Qi Guo
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took 301 under Professor Guo. Solid teacher, makes sure to pause for questions. Quizzes that he had were fair and takes very neat lecture notes in class. Overall would recommend to take 301 under Guo.

One of the best prof I've had at Purdue, and the best choice for 301. Exams are brutally hard but each exam is curved to a 75 average, and the class is curved ~10% on top of it! Beautiful lecture slides, and recorded! As long as you work hard and honestly, you will do well. If you have the option to take it with Guo - run, don't walk!

Very good professor who truly cares about student's learning. Lectures are engaging and he takes time to make sure the class is keeping up with him and to answer questions. Homework take a significant amount of time but exams are very similar to them. Exams are curved to 75%

301 is a tough class, and professor Guo was awesome at both making concepts easy to understand and the class fun and engaging. He's a super genuine person who truly cares about his students. I guess you could say that he's a *Guo*ted professor :^)

analysis.name: Kent Quanrud
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Generous curve. I did perfect on homeworks and exactly average on exams and ended with A-. Super friendly and helpful and accessible outside class. Really cares about you. Best prof I've had at Purdue. Very knowledgable and inspiring.

He teaches well and breaks down the concepts into smaller chunks, but everything else in this class is poor. He has his own textbook, which is riddled with math errors (good luck studying). Both HWs and Exams use only problems from the textbook. There is no diversity in assessing you. You have to grade your own HW, which the TA evaluates!?!

This 3-credit course is actually a 9-credit course in disguise: Probability and Random Processes, Algebraic Graph Theory, and Algorithm Design. Everything is so intertwined that it makes the material much harder to master. 
While the instructor is patient and passionate about teaching, the course pacing is simply indigestible.

Professor Quanrud is a great lecturer, and the class was enjoyable. There were a few hiccups (errors in the textbook, self-grading policy, etc.) but overall the course was well worth it. Would recommend taking a class with him in the future.

Look at the trend in Kent's reviews, undergrads complain bc his class is hard, and grad students unanimously love him. The reality is he teaches a hard topic, but he actually makes it intuitive. Beyond that, he's one of the most abundantly caring and available CS professors I had at Purdue, he's the kind of person who it is impossible to dislike

analysis.name: Xiaokang Qiu
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

review_highlights.comment: Actually the worst professor I've had at Purdue. The lectures make no sense and the course is very disorganized. The source code has bugs in it that make your work twice as difficult, and he can't debug his own code (it's another professor's work that he pawns off as his own, he couldn't be bothered to put in effort).
