The professor attacks you if you ask for an extension even though he didn't even release the assignment until much later. So in order to keep the original due dates, he makes 2 steps due the same week. He is condescending and will constantly remind you that you have poor time management skills even though it's his fault.

Tough course, graded by 12 quizzes (+1 dropped). Some quizzes rocked, others sucked horrifically. Inconsistent, either breezed through slides or took forever to explain one thing. I would appreciate the addition of programming assignments to lessen the impact of bad quiz grades.

During the lecture, he cannot explain everything clearly, his slides make no sense, and you can't really learn from his lecture. His project is a disaster, you have to debug for him(takes about a day) since his code is pretty buggy and I bet he didn't test his code before he publish it to the class. (Maybe he just can't find or fix his bug^^)

His lectures are not very helpful, and he comes off as insensitive and condescending to students. One student asks him for clear instructions on project on Piazza, he replied "we didn't mean to babysit." You should know what you're getting into before taking his 468/595/573, they're basically the same class, but you need to do more in 573.

analysis.name: Qifan Song
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He talks to the screen most of the class. Doesn't check if the class has understood the concepts or not.  He needs to improve his English fluency to teach and communicate well.  There's hardly any point taking this class if most of the time you are trying to decipher what he is saying

I signed up for this class and had to drop it. First of all, this professor's ability to explain the material is very limited. It is extremely difficult to follow his lectures. Also, he has a very thick accent. I am not a native speaker as well and I don't judge people easily, but I can easily say that he cannot communicate with the class at all.

Had him for a seminar class. Grade was basically entirely attendance (No A if you miss like 2 classes) and completion grades. Felt like a waste of time and you could tell he didn't really want to be there. Also talked quietly without a mic and is kinda hard to understand (OK English).

Dr. Song was very thorough in his lectures. He was prompt in his responses, reasonable to requests, and fair. I enjoyed his class. Other students may have had a negative experience with the content, but he did a good job making it easier to digest.
Classes are not very helpful, the textbook is much clearer. Exams and homework are easy, but homework is time-intensive (6-8 hours per week). Grading is lenient.

analysis.name: Timothy Reese
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
His lecture videos and forum answers often go off on entirely irrelevant tangents or around in circles, leaving you as clueless as when you started.

Necessary information is scattered in at least three different places for any given task, meaning you can never answer a question as is and must check for hidden a gotcha point deduction elsewhere.

This course was harder than expected in terms of busywork. I took this class 'flipped,' meaning we were expected to watch the lecture videos outside of class, and use class time as office hours (not ideal). Professor Reese was always willing and able to help explain, even outside of class time, and truly cared about the students. Gracious curve!

For the person who designed STAT350, he uses his own online textbook and it is excessively hard to read. The teaching videos are also just him reading from the PPT, this makes nothing better. The course expects me to spend 20 hours a week, so it adds up to 60 hours per week along with 2 other CS courses.

Very uninspiring lectures with heavy material but very little explanation. Homeworks were so much work and while linked to the course material felt slightly repetitive and more like busywork. Organisation of the course overall felt lacking and exams were needlessly easy and felt like they tested nothing

This class was way harder than it should've been. His lecture videos are so confusing I never watched them, I would like give the slides to Chat and have it explain it to me. The homework and computer assignments were annoying, but more annoying is in class worksheets that are not that relevant. You're just going to teach yourself.

analysis.name: Pam Porterfield
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 200 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Pam rambles a lot with her examples which are incomparable to homework. She consistently exceeds the class time. Her exams are NOTHING like the practice exams. EA's are not helpful and tedious. No curve even though the exam averages are around 50%. Recitations are useless. TA's have no idea what is going on and what Pam is doing. AVOID THIS CLASS!!

She sets you up to fail.  I did fine, but the tests are not a measure of your intelligence, they are a measure of your ability to rapidly regurgitate information on your sheet.  If the professor is somehow reading this, allow more time for test or shorten them, I know students who studied for hours and hours and knew the material who failed.

Lectures felt like her stating information rather than truly explaining it. Prof. Porterfield is notorious for gatekeeping resources, such as complete lecture slides or answers to review problems. You get to make a cheat sheet for exams though. To (barely) succeed, take time out of class to work on understanding the material.

I took this class online, so no clue how to do excel activities. Not allowed to go to in-person recitations because "the roof may fall in." Sentiment towards her is validated by her treatment of students- made one cry. I completed the evaluation weeks before due, submitted it a few hours late and she took 50%. (due finals week) Good luck with her.

This class is not too good. If you were great at AP stats, things will be great but if not, this class is difficult. The average on our second exam was a 67. She emphasizes the use of Excel but we can't actually use it on exams so it's conflicting. I recommend watching the prerecorded lecture videos instead of boilercast or going to class.

analysis.name: Rhodes Pinto
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It's clear professor Pinto cares about what he teaches, but for a speech class there were very little speeches. I felt like he graded me very harshly and didn't give good feedback. I also felt I lost points for not participating; however I spoke almost every class. Normally I'm very good at speeches but I felt cheated in this class.
Terrific professor. Clearly passionate about his students and the subject matter. Very open and welcoming classroom. Just do the readings, participate every now and then and you'll be fine.

I have talked to a lot of people, and they say not to take Dr. Pinto because he is kind of an odd guy. Whether or not that is true, he is very caring for his students and does his job well. No exams (unlike a lot of other SCLA classes) and only a few papers that he helps you with. Very fair when it comes to grading. Also, lots of playing Monopoly!!
the class was good and he was fair up until the final. i was exactly one point away from receiving the next grade up which was very frustrating. he refused to round me.

Good professor that definitely cares about his students. He can ramble during lectures but they are pretty easy to understand. No quizzes, but a few essays take up the majority of your grade. Reading homework every night but its never too much. Overall great professor that I would definitely take again if I could.

analysis.name: Rusi Taleyarkhan
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great professor but awful teaching strategy imo. Nothing is posted on Brightspace such as lecture notes. Brightspace was literally empty. Students are expected to attend lectures and take their own notes which makes it difficult sometimes (actually always) to follow up with the lecture. Doesn't offer help directly and relies on TAs for everything

One of the worst classes I have taken. Attended every lecture, but had to rely on the textbook for learning, which didn't cover any of the values we had to memorize for exams. I would recommend writing down everything he says and then memorize everything. Asks very niche, unfair questions, and doesn't care if the class does poorly.

Dr Taleyarkhan is a great professor. He is definitely eccentric and occasionally funny. He expects you to be in class therefore he doesn't post his notes. That said it shouldn't be an issue if you show up and take notes. His homeworks and exams can prove tedious but all in all its a pretty easy class. Definitely learned a lot about nuclear eng.
No class notes posted, no homework solutions posted, talks without mic in class, no study guides, no past exams. Nearly impossible to study for this class

Brightspace page is completely empty: no lecture notes, no lecture videos, and no syllabus posted. This makes it extremely hard to study as if you miss one class you are missing tons of information. Also he heavily relies on TAs for almost everything, first exam took over a month to grade. Overall he needs to get with the times and embrace tech

analysis.name: Sayed Soleimani
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Exams are very difficult, and don't correlate to the notes. He tends to rant a lot in lecture especially about people who don't come to class, which is annoying bc he's talking to the people who are there. He gets upset if people don't know how to solve things and blames the bad averages on students 'not studying enough.' He "loses his appetite."

Dr. Soleimani takes himself and his class very seriously. I see lots of ratings for his higher level courses, and I fully believe that he is a solid professor for those. For CE270, his exams and averages have been extremely tough, to the point that even our TA's have asked him to make exams shorter, but he fully blames the class for low grades.

This professor frequently speaks about how the student's confusion disgusts him and causes him to 'lose his appetite,' although the confusion stems from the fact that the lectures do not correlate with the exams and that the homework is genuinely impossible to do well on. No amount of studying could make you prepared for exams. Never again.

He is very knowledgable in his field and is good at lectures. However, the exams were outrageous, they were so much harder than any lecture or homework assignment, having you solve problems in a way that you have never done before and having no way to prepare for that level. I failed the class just because of how heavy the exams were weighted.

I found this class to be unreasonably hard. The homeworks were impossible to get above a C on. During our 8:30 am lecture, the prof would frequently yell at the class about the majority who weren't there. TAs were unhelpful and rude during exams.

analysis.name: Tridib Saha

review_highlights.comment: This is a tough course and honestly Prof Saha's lectures and prerecorded videos helped getting me the A. Those who claim otherwise are usually bad students.

Unhelpful prof with a huge ego who talks down to his students. Online resources and TAs were more useful for learning material than he was. Made the structure of the course drastically different from the main campus (ie, 3 midterms instead of 2, FRQ instead of MC), though the courses are supposed to be the same on both campuses. Avoid this prof.

Tells us just because he can finish the exam in 10 mins so we should be able to do it in 60 like he wasn't the one who wrote it

Honestly, the worst professor I've had at Purdue. I did well in the class, but Saha is unreasonably hostile, makes fun of struggling students who ask questions often by questioning their intelligence, and has a massive ego. If Saha is meant to represent ECE in Indianapolis, he needs to get in check. Also got caught with porn. Shady person overall.

analysis.name: Troy Seagraves
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great professor for SCLA102. He's a pretty young professor so he's very cheerful and nice to talk to. He's super into the topics he teaches and so his lectures are enjoyable. Two impromptu speeches (which are pretty easy) and two big group projects (which are easy if you have a good group). If you go to class, and do the reading, it's an easy A.

Unlike most professors I had this semester, Dr. Seagraves isn't a boring lecturer who talks in a monotonous tone but rather is very engaging. He also goes out of his way to learn EVERY student's name. Seagraves is always willing to help you understand concepts. However, there is a lot of reading, and he may grade a bit harsh on some speeches.

He certainly cares a lot about the course he teaches and goes out of his way to engage with the class and know his students. The biggest complaint is we had projects for his class run into the middle of finals week, which felt like a bit much. Do the reading, and when giving speeches, body language is key.

Really engaging professor, he draws your attention really well and actually cares about each and every student. Phones are not allowed in class which helps with engagement.  Uses all 50 minutes to a maximize, amazing professor

analysis.name: Sarah Sellke
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 78 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Selke is smart and values students, but struggles with clear teaching. Lectures repeat basics but gloss over complex concepts. HW/Exam questions have multiple interpretations, but no clarity on which interpretation is correct, causing confusion. Students' concerns about this on the class board are met with some variation of "stop complaining"

I would never take her class again. A nice person, but with childish teaching style. A lot of HW each week. Exams are most from HW and you really need to memory a lot of things. Got one part wrong, you lose the whole points. Grading toughly. If you like tough class, go ahead. But if you are just a normal student, she would not be my first choice.

I gave a 2 cuz she's not a mean person nor does she have bad intentions. But, as sweet as she may be, she is NOT a good professor. She's a terrible lecturer, our hw is either on topics "out of scope" of the course or requires hours of drawing, and exams are graded terribly as well, with any concerns or regrade requests considered as "complaints".

Surely there is a better way to go about explaining sorting algorithms, which we have been doing for a quarter of the semester at this point. The oversimplified explanations are deceptive, given that you realise you did not understand any of it by the end of the lecture. Given how pivotal this course is to CS majors, I would expect greater clarity.

This class has taught me patience more than anything else. You might ask what you learn throughout this course. The answer is SORTING and more importantly how to solve technical issues that she faces during the class. Oh, and you will learn a lot about technical interview questions such as "the difference between arrays and arraylists."

analysis.name: Marcus Thompson

He's the worst teacher I've ever had!!! A total disaster who can't form a single coherent thought. He drifts through class like a clueless ghost. His “teaching” is a joke. He doesn't grade, doesn't communicate, barely shows up, always late, even for exams. Calling him unprofessional is generous.

Thompson is knowledgeable for sure, but he's a very poor communicator. He's not great at lecturing. He mostly just feels like he thinks he's teaching freshman high school students rather than juniors and seniors. God I miss Hands

No grades were returned until 2 days before the semester ended. Gave grades for an "Exam 2" that was planned at the start of the semester but he forgot to implement so everyone just got 100%. Labs are just stolen from other online sources. Slides are mostly brainrot memes and Twitter posts. Easy A I guess since you learn absolutely nothing

Students in 323 and 581 also say those courses are complete, utter failures. How do you inherit 4 well-structured courses from amazing, accomplished professors and ruin all 4? He gave lectures on how to give good course evals for his courses btw. Asked for feedback since 2024 but classes have only gotten worse. Glad he's no longer teaching 470.

analysis.name: Stacy Zuelly
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Llectures are great and super organized, very easy to follow. All the information is given to you that is needed for exams and quizzes. However, she made the whole class buy a physical iclicker instead of using the app on our phones. This was a bit ridiculous because they were pretty pricey at $50, and that could have been avoided withe the app.

Dr. Zuelly is an excellent professor whose passion makes labs both informative and fun. Her policies may seem strict, but are fair and help you become a better student. Even if not required, I'd highly recommend her class to any Animal Science undergraduate student. 10/10 would take again in a heartbeat!

Dr. Zuelly is an amazing professor, and I highly recommend taking her classes. Attendance is mandatory, but if you don't have any absences, you are able to opt out of the final exam! At the end of each lecture and lab there is a mini quiz, and if you paid attention during class, you will be fine!

Professor Zuelly's class had clear expectations and was not difficult. It was nice to not have final exams with 100% attendance throughout the semester as well. I was not a fan of her as a person. She has a lot of grace for herself and her own mistakes (which happen a lot) but is very strict on her students. Class is easy, but she's not kind.

This class was pretty easy but not very lax on any missing attendance. Attendance is required and there are NO drops or points that you can earn back for missing class. Zuelly is very funny, and I really enjoyed her class, but you really cannot miss much before your grade starts going down.

analysis.name: Uli Walther
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He breaks down very difficult abstract concepts very well, connects with other areas of mathematics and never makes anyone feel bad for a question. Brilliant to talk to outside of class and has interesting perspectives to offer mathematics as a whole. Exams were easy so one can engage as much as they wish with the course content.

Professor Walther is an amazing lecturer who goes about teaching math really well. Calc 3 honors was a great experience for me as he is very clear on the concepts he teaches. He encourages questions and answers very precisely with some humor thrown in. There's a lot of content taught, so pay attention to homework and lectures. Also practice.

Uli's an amazing guy to talk to, but I normally had to read the textbook or watch a video to understand what was going on in lecture. However, he was great at responding to questions, so definitely know what to ask and take advantage of the small class size. Also, the final wasn't cumulative, but exams were still very hard.

Uli was such an amazing professor. You can tell he's very smart and passionate about math. I took the honors section of this class just for the small class size and better grading. In this class homework is 40% of your grade and quizzes are 15% which was really nice to cushion the exam grades.

Overall, I really enjoyed the class. Be prepared to spend time outside of class to go to office hours if needed, since the content will be somewhat difficult, especially towards the end of the semester. Class sizes are small, and you can attend the other section's lecture if needed.

analysis.name: Bernd Ulrich
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Not generous with partial credit, so small mistakes on exams can cost you big-time in this class. The final exam was worth 200/600 points in the class, and it was difficult. Homeworks were to be turned in in-person in paper form, which was inconvenient. Lectures were just him writing out definitions and theorems and proofs- not super helpful.

Very nice professor, impeccable lecture notes. However (maybe because it's a grad class) he doesn't post lecture notes which forces into an attendance mandatory class. Exams are pretty tough. Otherwise, he is one of the better profs out there, definitely recommend him for other classes.

Lectures are directly from lecture notes posted on Brightspace. Exams were mostly quite easy but with some tricky multiple-choice questions. HW is overwhelmingly easy but could be a bit more reflective of the exam content.
Very caring. For HWs, he basically put emphasis on computation, which is not very helpful for understanding.

Amazing professor. Material is structured based on the standard text for this course but he makes his own revisions which are quite helpful (clearer proofs, more precise notation). Explains everything thoroughly in lecture and tries to actually develop intuition for the theorems. Exams consist of few questions but aren't unreasonably difficult.

analysis.name: Pramey Upadhyaya
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He explains all problems in-depth and is a great recitation professor. He does make time to help you after class if you have questions.

Prof. Upadhyaya is an excellent 2k1 recitation professor. His recitations have just the right mix of lecture review and example problems. He's an excellent explainer, breaks down difficult examples/concepts well, and takes time to answer questions thoroughly. Highly recommend his section for 2k1.

While this class is notorious for having exam averages in the 40s, Prof Upadhyaya really did his best in explaining the material. He recorded his lectures,broke down concepts slowly, worked out examples, and even did supplementary recordings when students had questions. His explanations really made things click, even if the test material was hard

He is by far one of the nicest professors I have ever had. He is extremely accessible outside the class and is very approachable. His teaching pace is also perfect and you will understand everything clearly if you pay attention. He doesnt mind slowing down and repeating concepts should people need him to. Get this professor, you wont regret it!

Such a gem of a prof. Lectures aren't mandatory, but lecture + book  much better understanding. Won't hesitate to re-explain material. Make sure to read the book. Exams are fair, but tough for sure. Most of my respect for him comes from his exam review lectures, which he'll go for as long as needed to go over all the material. Love him

analysis.name: Ryan Umbeck
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Umbeck is one of the best professors at Purdue. Even during a 7:30am class, he still brought energy and engagement to each lecture that made the content easy to follow and understand. The course material can get a little confusing at times, but Dr. Umbeck goes over everything in great detail and answers questions perfectly.

Making an entry-level statistical inference course interesting is a very difficult task, but Professor Umbeck has a bright and encouraging energy that makes you want to pay attention simply out of respect for the effort he is putting into making the material understandable. Fantastic person, gives great feedback on issues with Stata HW (use him!).

I really enjoyed his class. He does not require attendance yet most of the class still shows up every day because he makes the subject so interesting. I wasn't sure about econ until I took this class.
One of the nicest professors at Purdue and teaches really well because he genuinely cares about the subject.
One of the best professor in Purdue. Always patient to students, answer questions on time.

analysis.name: Laura Urba
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I really like Prof. Urba. She does have a bit of an accent but it's not very distracting after a bit. She explains things pretty well and is very open to questions. Attendance is "mandatory", but you only have to be there half of the time she takes attendance and she tells you ahead of time when those are. My lab TAs were also very helpful.

She's such a nice professor! Before class, she always made sure to talk to students and give us all advice. Lectures are amazing. Exams allow a cheat sheet (front and back) and her lecture slides are impeccable to study from. Glad she was my professor because she inspired me to take on a minor in statistics.

Professor Urba did a great job at teaching this course. While the slides do include derivations, they are very important to build intuition to the real physics at play. She stresses key ideas over memorizing formulae, which is the best way to truly learn the material. Exams were very fair and the course is very well structured. Totally recommend.

Maybe I'm slow but the lectures were kind of hard to grasp, especially the derivation heavy ones, so I ended up not paying attention off during the derivation parts since you don't need them for exam (I know, bad mentality). I ended up self studying the entire course myself which is not fun. On the bright side she's energetic and passionate!

Prof. Urba is such a kind lecturer, but at times her lectures are boring and hard to engage with. Love love love Wasserman. He's so kind and you can tell he cares so much about the students. You need an 85% to get an A, with 3-4 dropped quizzes and either 1 dropped midterm or half-dropped final. Only necessary attendance is Friday quizzes, every week. Would recommend actually doing the reading, but it's not checked. Overall loved the class!

Dr. Wasserman is da GOAT. He wants to get to know and his lectures have amazing demos and clear notes. You only need an 85 to get an A and he lets you drop 4 quizzes, 1 midterm or half the final, and 1 lab. Dr. Wasserman sets you up very well for higher level chem no matter if you plan to go into grad, medical, dental, or whatever career!

Dr. Wasserman was probably one of my favorite professors this semester. He's really creative with his lectures and is happy to answer any questions that his students have. The only thing that gets me are the Friday quizzes, which can be a bit stressful at times to prepare for. There's a lot of outside work, however. But Wasserman is awesome!

analysis.name: Adam Baxmeyer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I had him for 459. Baxmeyer is not a bad prof. Decent lecturer, and good guest speakers. I've never really reviewed professors on here, but if you have Tim as your TA, you might as well just drop the class. When nobody in the class can get above a C on an essay the entire semester, you might as well just take another class. Don't waste your time.

One of my favorite professors within the aviation department. I feel like I learned a lot from his course, yet overall, it did not feel difficult. His grading is lenient as long as you try, and he is clearly passionate about aviation.

Adam is a nice guy and very knowledgeable. He's actively working as an airport director so is a gokd resource for job specific information. It's very lecture heavy and sometimes they can get boring. Would recommend taking his class

analysis.name: Adam Bodony
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Bodony is a great conductor and gives very clear, concise feedback. He makes a lot of jokes in rehearsals and has a deep knowledge of musical history.

Professor Bodony was my favorite Purdue professor, and all-time favorite orchestra conductor. He is caring, empathetic and passionate about his students and their success. College is not easy for many, and he makes it known that he is there for his students. He is a great leader for the orchestras and music department as a whole.

Professor Bodony is a great orchestra director, and I really enjoyed all of the rehearsals. He is a very good conductor, and I like the advice he gives to make our pieces sound better. Show up to class (that is what your graded on) and enjoy.

I wanted to continue playing violin so I signed up for orchestra. Bodony does a good job picking fun music to play and providing helpful feedback, but I don't feel passionate about playing my instrument. I like that you're not graded for how well you perform so there's no pressure but sometimes that extra push can make music all the more rewarding.

Professor Bodony is an amazing guy. In the chaos of the coronavirus, he has been nothing but caring and understanding of how weird everything is for us right now. The first day of the semester, he gave a speech that made me tear up - acknowledging that our lives are strange right now, but as musicians we have the ability to escape through music

analysis.name: Jacob Adler
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: My only qualm with this class is that your grade is heavily dependent on what TA you have. I've heard great things about some TAs, while I had one would tell us blatantly wrong information. The lab itself is incredibly easy and as long as you try you will get an A. Make sure you have a good lab group or you will do a lot of extra work.

I am currently a freshman in bio 135 and 121 and Professor Jacob is a great professor. While the lab is mostly ran by TA/TIs, the lecture is ran by Jacob. All of the teaching team is amazing and wants you to succeed. My best advice is to show up for class and ask questions when you have them. Overall both courses are great!!!

Had JJ Adler for both bio 121 and bio 135. Really cares about his students, both academically and personally. He even sends personalized follow-up emails to your questions/concerns in forms. Lectures are clear 99% of the time. No textbooks. Only bad thing is you have to go "feasting with faculty" for office hours instead of normal office hours.

The learning goals could have gone better, and the criteria could have been clearly. The DNA analysis weeks were cool, but dirt is kind of boring. Overall the course was designed with good intentions but didn't have great execution. Good intro to college biology lab but glad to be done.

Dr. Adler is incredibly sweet and caring, but I have also heard that when it comes to grading, this class is very TA dependent. My TAs were nice, but some on Reddit mention how it felt like their TAs were out to get them. Make sure to attend the lectures and labs, reach out to Dr. Alder if you are struggling, and genuinely put in effort!

analysis.name: Adeola Mobolaji
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Mobolaji was the best professor I have had at Purdue so far. He is so passionate about the course and knows that most of us are there just because it's required so his main goal is "just listen to your classmates and learn." (He says that a lot). It's hard not to get an A in this course. Take him if you can get him!

Professor Mobolaji is super chill and always happy. He really wants the best for his students, and he is very understanding of his students. He grades super easy and gives amazing feedback. He lets students re-do presentations with no penalty if they blank the first time. He promotes a fun and stress-free environment. He is a great com professor.

Class was organized despite a few last minute changes. Lots of busy work assignments with few that are actually going to make you better at presentations. Finding live audiences is a bit of a hassle so make sure to be ready.
Very easy class and even nicer professor. Makes coming to class enjoyable and will respect your time and values. I would recommend taking any class that he teaches.

He truly represents what every teacher should strive to be. He cares about each students improvement and makes a direct effort to connect with all those in his class. He is my favorite professor on my schedule. Best guy!

analysis.name: Adam Kotanko
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Most caring professor I've ever had. You attend class and email your group's discussion summary for credit every class (hence "mandatory" attendance). You get plenty skips for when you're sick, and he provides extensive feedback on your submissions. He has a passion in teaching and is a very understanding instructor. Very light coursework.

He's a great teacher that doesn't believe in exams/quizzes, but rather testing through group discussions, projects, and film reviews. In fact, he is just a grad student, but compared to my friends who had full professors that just lectured and gave exams, I still learned way more. If you take Mr. Kotanko he will make you a better person.

Kotanko is an extremely kind and understanding professor. He prompts you to think beyond the surface-level appearance of society. He has great communication and his respect for his students is evident. I would love the chance to take one of his classes again.

This is the best professor at Purdue. He is so caring and genuinely gets to know each of his students. He is understanding and wants to see you succeed. He is not a hard grader at all. This is the best professor and class ever.

Seriously the sweetest professor I've ever had. This is a really easy class the only way you'll fall behind is if you skip a lot of classes. Technically attendance isn't mandatory (if you're really sick he'll understand) but points are given for discussions so you really have to pay attention to those but you can always make them up. 4 get dropped.

analysis.name: Adam Huffield

review_highlights.comment: The content itself is useful if you're into strength and conditioning, and the required textbook is solid, but don't expect much empathy or room for individual circumstances. If you're a student who might need any type of flexibility, this class might be more stress than it's worth. Grading is harsh, and he won't give you feedback.

The lectures were more of a group discussion then a lecture, and you were graded on how often you showed up and participated. This grade was a HARSH grade, so be sure that you not only show up to every single class and lab, but also actively participate in the discussions held. Adam shared good info from his experience as an RD in the "real world."

Adam does reverse-classroom style formatting so you will read the textbook/look over his PowerPoint before coming to class and then have a big group discussion during class. He creates a welcoming classroom environment and shares his experiences in the field. Awesome professor.

analysis.name: Adam Watkins

review_highlights.comment: There's a lot of writing in a short amount of time, but if you're okay with that, the retreat is a very valuable experience and Dr. Watkins does a really good job of engaging with his students. I would highly recommend going on this retreat if you're an Honors student.

About a quarter of students' grades are based on peer evaluations. Weekly readings are fairly long, (especially for a 1-credit hour class), but the associated discussion posts are very easy to get full credit on. I took Dr. Watkins "Homegrown" class this last fall semester, as well as taking one of his HONR 19901 classes. He is such a wonderful teacher, and he genuinely cares about his students. I had no problem with coming to his office hours with my questions about his assignments, and he always gave back clear feedback and made everything make sense.

Lectures are very one-sided, as he tends to be very insistent on his own viewpoints, despite preaching being affirmative and open-minded. He gives very unclear feedback, and is an unnecessarily harsh grader for it being a 1 credit class, taking off points without indicating why just because he can't bring himself to give someone a 100%.
Very respectful, very kind. This class requires a lot of participation. He provides articles to read, but no purchases necessary. Really will help your leadership grow. Not a difficult class.

analysis.name: Ahmed Idrissi Alami

review_highlights.comment: Noo one better than Dr. Idrissi to teach anything about Arab culture. I took many classes with him and it is clear he cares about the learning of all his students. I really enjoyed Prof. Idrissi Alami's class, you can tell that he is extremely passionate about what he teaches. He is knowledgeable and well respected. I appreciated all the time he dedicated to making the class worthwhile. A good amount of reading, but just do the work and you should be fine.
English fluency is mediocre. Uses lots of lecturing and little to no interactive activities. Goes off topic often and seems disroganized.
Professor seems to be profiling Non-American students.

I really enjoyed Prod. Alma's class. Sure, theres a lot of reading, but if you do the reading and are prepared for class you have nothing to worry about. Had some really great discussions in this class that got me interested in the subject even further.

review_highlights.comment: She really cares about her students and what she teaches; but, she expects students to know everything she says in lecture verbatim for her quizzes and exams. I liked CHM281 - but it can be ridiculous at times. She is the harshest grader I've ever had, wants you to know exactly the answer she wants, and remember every detail from lecture. Hardest class I've ever met. Could not just get a single A through whole semester. Always tested things outside the review sheet. And the professor is such a hard grader who pick on too many details in the answer. And too many things to remember for a quiz or a critique.

Please do not take this class. The content was interesting but your grades will be based on how the professor feels about you. If you are on her good side then you will obtain a good grade, however, if you find yourself on the other side let's hope you really work hard because a B will be your highest grade. Worst class experience I have ever had.

One of my favorite professors at Purdue! Although I'm a little bias with loving to write, she was very flexible with due dates, creative ideas, and always had a smile on her face! 1000% suggest her

analysis.name: AJ Schwichtenberg

You do have to come to class because there are quizzes everyday over the assigned readings, but there is no final because of this. Also there isn't a textbook.

She always made sure that her lectures were as engaging and easy to understand as possible. She was always willing to answer questions and re-explain concepts if people were confused. It is clear that she is passionate about what she is teaching which made the class even more enjoyable. She was always available to talk outside of class.

If you are going into clinical psych, therapy, or working with children, you NEED to take this class. She does amazing in-person activities to learn about assessment methods, interventions, and dealing with children. My favorite class at Purdue, go to class and pay attention to get an A. Exams are easy if you study the slides and study guides.

She is one of the best professors I have had at Purdue. Very engaging lectures and a very interesting subject matter. It is clear she cares about the subject and her students learning the subject. This class is an easy A if you show up to lectures, do the assignments, and put in even minimal effort studying for exams. Overall highly recommend!

analysis.name: Ajith Rajapaksha
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Ajith is the worst professor that I have ever experienced in my 15 years of education, (and I've had some bad teachers). Be ready to teach yourself every single thing in this class, because if you ask him a question, even a simple yes or no question he will go out of his way to make you feel like the dumbest person on the planet.

Ajith was by far the worst professor I've had at Purdue.  He was always rude to students in and out of class.  He refused to explain his poorly written syllabus even when directly asked.  The grading is very confusing and difficult.  He only teaches this class, yet he's almost never available.  Even during office hours, he won't want to talk.

Ajith gets to know all his students names and tries to encourage them to put in the extra effort to really understand physics. His grading is harsh and at times convoluted and difficult to grasp, which turns many students off. I think if he simplified his grading and gave students a little more slack he'd be a really great professor.

4 HW sets a week, Graded by how you use his  methods. If you don't write out your answer the way he wants it, you could possibly fail your assignment, even if you got it 100% correct. It is absolute BS. Stay away. I was an A grader in my A Level College Physics but I got a C in this class, which was relatively much easier.
He changed the syllabus to his liking, making it much more difficult. He stops grading after a tiny mistake. He can even consider a 90% a fail. If you're taking him for PHYS 218, please change.

analysis.name: Akshath Jitendranath
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: not accessible outside of class. doesnt put in grades on time. discussions jump from topic to topic without any clear discourse. doesnt reply to emails. have to remind him multiple times. No proper feedback - told me I did a good job, but gave me an 90. removed the syllabus, so now there is no proper guidance. lack of standardized grading - AVOID.

Unlike other SCLA classes, this isn't an easy A. No RUBRIC whatsoever. Vague instructions and thinks he teaches us important lessons, but it's a bunch of yap. Try not to fall asleep challenge: level impossible. He will argue against you if it doesn't align with his beliefs. RUN, don't just walk away from the class and Jitendranath. You're welcome.

Don't expect an A — he flat out refuses to give them. No rubrics for presentations, so you're guessing what he wants. Very few assignments but tons of reading. The saving grace? Class is actually fun because it's all open discussion on controversial topics, and he lets everyone share their views without bias. Great debates, brutal grading.

Even though he may seem like a tough grader at times, to put it in his own words he wants to "light a fire in your a**", so if you take his feedback seriously and try your best you will definitely get a solid grade. His lectures are extremely entertaining and the books discussed in class are very interesting. I would recommend his class to anyone

Jitendranath is a fantastic lecturer who possesses a passion for economics.

That aside, he's a tough grader who doesn't believe in rubrics, so grades are extremely subjective. It took too long to learn this since there wasn't a grade inputted until week 12. 

You'll learn a lot in this class, but avoid it if you care about your grade.

Great Professor!

Osumi-sensei is really an exceptional teacher. She makes class very interesting and engaging, and is very forgiving with grades. On top of that, the course content is interesting and helpful for any students taking Japanese. I highly recommend this course.

Osumi-sensei truly cares about teaching Japanese effectively, which you see through her preparation for class every day, and the level of engagement she provides. She answers any questions and provides clear instructions. Although there is a decent amount of work through LJO (the textbook), it is necessary to learn the language well.
She cares about student study, althougn there is a lots of homework but it was easy. Strongly recommended, and there is a lots of extra credit activity can attend.
She really cares about you! Fun and interactive classes, would definitely take her classes again!

One of the best professors I have ever had! She was so enthusiastic! She loves teaching and is great at clarifying everything. She really makes sure students understand the material. Wonderful Professor!

Over zoom its easy to forget youre in a class but she used cute pictures and had songs for every unit. Japanese is a tough language to learn (as a native English speaker) so obviously this class will require lots of work. Love her :)
Probably one of the most fun, informative, and enthusiastic professors I have ever had the privilege of being a student of.

Expect to get called on randomly, but it's low pressure and she doesn't judge.

Love her! Had for both JPNS101 & 102. I always looked forward to her class, she makes language learning enjoyable! She can explain concepts simply & answer questions!

I'm taking an intensive summer course with her (basically a year of Japanese in 2 months) and I couldn't ask for a better professor. An open-minded instructor. She will not blame you and guide you instead when you make a mistake. You can also communicate with or email her at any time with any Japanese-related topics. She will be glad to reply. After-class Japanese events are also welcomed. Also, very loose grading policy. An easy A or A+ if you just spent little time on it.

Shes the best! What I liked most about her is how well she gets to know her students. Even by the middle of the semester she knew our majors, where we were from, and other details about us. Shes my favorite professor Ive had so far at Purdue and Im genuinely sad that I wont be able to have her for a third semester.
