Really passionate about what he teaches, but because of his EE background, he goes way too in-depth on topics and rambles a lot during class. Exams are extremely hard even if you study and class has over 1000 slides for the final exam.  Too much material crammed into one course imo which makes retaining knowledge on what was taught difficult.

While Prof. Adams is clearly passionate about what he teaches and is a generally good lecturer, he has by far some of the WORST tests I have ever seen. Focuses on testing whether you remember obscure trivia rather than if you truly understand the material. Furthermore, the tests are structured to be ambiguous and an english comprehension test.

analysis.name: Allison Schaser
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I loved Dr. Schaser and this class. The material was very interesting and the labs were fun. Dr. Schaser is so kind and helpful and always helped in office hours! Study hard for the tests because they make a big chunk of the grade!
This professor is very kind and answers emails quickly. The class itself is pretty difficult. The homework is easy and doesn't take long. The tests are very dense and takes a lot of time to learn.

Dr. Schaser is a decent professor, but this course material is pretty dense and there is a lot to work with. Hw assignments are easy and there are 5 a week, but tests can be pretty brutal if you don't study.

analysis.name: Chad Allred
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: You either like him or don't. He spends much of class rambling on about personal stories. Test content is purely from the textbook. Much of the course is creating worksheets or content for a client which does give great practical and hands on experience. He's a good enough professor to make the class worth it.
He does not teach in class. Only talks about his experiences and his exposure, and what he has done and learnt. Literally never mentions the textbook but all midterms are based on the textbook.

Chad is an overall nice guy who tries, but it is not enough. He really emphasizes "WOW" points, but he never gives them for the teams, and it is counted out of your grade at the end of the semester. My group did everything he said to do, on time, properly, and went above expectations. With a 0/50, my grade was 5% lower than it should've been!!

Chad is so sweet and genuine, but as a teacher he doesn't do much. Exams are so tough, but I found out that it's all copied from textbook questions so it's all on Quizlet (!!!). Lectures is all him telling stories and about him, so he doesn't teach. The semester project is awesome though and really enjoyed it, it was great experience.

If you have the option, DO NOT JOIN HIS CLASS. The professor & his TAs are ridiculous when it comes to grading. They don't even read the full paper & won't give back points even when they admit they're wrong. This happened to all the groups in my class and we were outraged. If you follow their rubrics, you only get 50-75% of points.

analysis.name: Alex Psomas
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Good professor overall and breaks complex topics down well. The one downside is that he expects a high level of prior knowledge coming into the class and will skip steps in his notes because of that.

Prof Psomas and CS 381 is what any CS class should be like. Amazing lectures, structured homeworks, informative slides, and fair exams. Is the class hard and going to make you want to jump in frozen wabash river? Yes. Is the class very interesting with a top-notch lecturer? Also yes. Would 100% recommend no matter your CS interests.

381 is a very difficult class due to the amount of time you need to put in it along with tough exams. He lectures very well and can answer questions with good examples too. The curve was pretty big at the end.

Tough class, great professor. He definitely cares about your learning on a subject that many people just can't grasp. TA's were kinda harsh though and graded very strictly. But if you go to Psoma's lectures, you will get a good understanding of the material.
Best cs lecturer I have had at purdue. Course is tough but worth taking it.

analysis.name: Alec Rhodes
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Rhodes was great. You must talk in class to earn participation points, but he grades everything super easily. He wants to see you succeed, and he offers extra credit if you wear business attire during presentations. There is a lot of reading for the class, and then all you do during class is discuss. GET READY TO PRESENT!

Great professor! I took him for SCLA 102. Lectures are pretty chill, although you have to participate. Really caring professor, if you need help definitely reach out to him he's super kind and helpful. Attendance and participation are a good amount of your grade. Overall super easy grader and cool professor. Would take again!

I had the best experience with Mr. Rhodes. His teaching style is one you can easily adapt to, and he is truly passionate about the work he assigns. He's very open and straightforward about the ciriculum so feel free to ask questions. Would most definitely take again!
Great Professor. Definitely recommend for SCLA 102. Makes lectures engaging and interesting. Have to participate in class but it's not daunting. No exams, but be ready to present.

analysis.name: Alex Hsu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Good professor; his homework truly helps you with the exams. His advice is also helpful - do the homework in practice mode so you can truly grasp the content. attendance mandatory. I will say that sometimes it's a bit hard to follow him - be ready to learn the content outside of class. had to teach myself over 5 lessons.
He is very clear and explains content super well. His class is not hard at all and the practice exam review questions are life-savers. He kept things simple and is overall fantastic.
Very clear and direct. Provides great instruction and is always willing to answer questions. Did not struggle with this class at all, even though I did bad in precalc/trig

analysis.name: Alex Pothen
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Pothen is alright. It really feels like he wants students to understand by going through some of the more intriguing applications of numerical analysis. BUT beware of his iClicker quizzes if u wanna skip his classes and cram before midterms (def achievable). Overall a sweet guy but holy crap the handwriting reflects on his monotone voice.

Lectures are very interesting but can be hard to follow at times. I believe he is a kind hearted man. Many concepts in the class are much easier than they seem at first. The explanations for topics on the homeworks and in lectures can be excessive / ineffective at times.

He's a caring professor and he's knowledgeable about 314.
I think his lectures are ok in person but he mumbles quite a bit, making lecture recordings really hard to understand. He also uploads notes, which are hard to understand (better than nothing though).
Homeworks can be tedious, but aren't super hard. Exams are fair. Grades/curved leniently
Lectures have little to no value as he mumbles a lot, and his work is hard to follow. Learning the material on your own is required.

Prof Pothen is a nice and understanding person, giving us a few days of deadline for homework and an extra 10 minutes on the 2nd midterm. The lectures are not easy to follow although the content itself isn't hard. My only complaint is that homework is too tedious. Can take anywhere from 6 to 9 hours.

analysis.name: Andrei Gabrielov
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 79 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Gabrielov's like that sweet old grandad you have. The kind tries to teach you things but in the end you don't really know what he's saying and end up smiling and nodding at everything. Now imagine that grandad being Russian. Needless to say, I didn't understand much of what he said and just like at family dinners, I excused myself and left.

Basically the wacky uncle of the Math department. He seems like a very friendly person, but he skips steps in example problems, is very difficult to understand (thick accent), and doesn't explain new material very well. He may also be a Soviet sleeper cell, but that's based more on suspicion than evidence.

As lecturer, Gabrielov does not excel. He has a moderately thick russian accent, and when combined with a small amount of background noise and a low quality microphone he can be hard to understand in lecture halls.  His strengths lie in face to face interactions. He is extremely intelligent and resolve any issues you have with course material.

Absolutely terrible. So hard to understand, skips steps all the time, and writes really hard tests. Going to class with Gabrielov isn't even worth it. I survived through using the internet, but it was not a good experience. Avoid taking at all costs.

His handwriting is very bad, he reuses paper so you can see work on the other side, his accent is difficult at times, his lectures have NO structure whatsoever and he blames students for his own mistakes and says 'you need to watch what I'm doing and tell me if I make a mistake'. If you get him, watch other lectures on BoilerCast. Good luck...

analysis.name: Andrew Bellisari
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Kindest, most passionate professor I have had. Attendance is mandatory but you will want to show up to every class. It was incredibly fun, and he is an amazing person to be around. I'd definitely take this class again if I could. The content was engaging, and his lectures were even more so.

Professor Bellisari is absolutely amazing. While attendance is mandatory, this is a class that you will want to attend. He is incredibly well spoken during his lectures and extremely kind to his students. If you have the opportunity, absolutely take a class he is teaching. Hist 408

As a STEM major, I fully expected SCLA 102 to be a snooze-fest, but professor Bellisari made every period engaging and interesting. Our class discussions were wide-ranging and incredibly thought-provoking, everything we did felt motivated and intentional, and prof. Bellisari consistently made an effort to switch things up to keep things interesting

Professor Bellisari was one of the best professors I had last semester. He's a very engaging speaker and managed to make 75 minute class periods go by quickly. I'm not the biggest fan of public speaking, but on speech days, he made the classroom a calm and encouraging environment where I didn't feel super nervous about presenting.

Professor Bellisari's class was engaging, with frequent discussions on the readings. He doesn't check if you've read but expects participation. Grading was unusual, as he completed it all on the last day before grades were due. He is lenient with grading. Be ready for pop quizzes, but they are fairly basic so spark notes should be enough.

analysis.name: Andrew Toms
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 95 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Only thing that could make him better would be if he was right handed
Wore a pickachu hat to lecture once you could say he's a pretty cool guy. Most of the time his lectures on last about 20 minutes.

Toms is a pretty funny/entertaining guy.  He always throws in some jokes or goes on a funny rant during lectures.  He also writes the exams to be very easy.  His teaching skills are just average in my opinion.  He uses the same examples in lecture that are used in the textbook and tends not to fully explain the key concepts.

Doesn't waste any time. Gives you exactly what you need for exams. He wasn't even my prof and I went to all his lectures anyway outside of the first week. He's also hilarious in a kind of out of pocket way, which is awesome.

Solid lecturer, but can go too fast at times and the class information is tough. Something this professor could do better is repeating important information. Stories were funny, and made the lectures better.

analysis.name: Lynda Aouar
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She does not answer any emails sent to her Very difficult to understand and writes very lightly on the board so that it is not readable. Late to class and doesn't tell students when there are review sessions. lets students create a cheat sheet but it doesnt really help Seems lost about the course herself, gets things wrong and doesnt know due dates

No control over her own classroom. Constantly confused by everything - computers, brightspace, questions, her own lectures, her assigned due dates. Typos in notes, 4 exam questions were graded incorrectly. Didn't think through any assignments, had to make things up on the spot when asked about it. Didn't give lectures of topics in time for 2nd exam

Unable to answer questions about the material and gets defensive and condescending. Fails to pace curriculum well. Unaware of her own due dates. Tests and quizzes contain errors and take forever to get graded. Unprepared for classes. Has errors on slides. Struggles with Brightspace. Does not communicate necessary info in time. The list goes on...

Has no idea what is going on within her own class. Unable to answer questions, and will belittle students for questioning her responses, even if they are incorrect. Will not respond to emails, and no clarity on what current grades are. Quizzes and exams are graded incorrectly and take numerous weeks to return. Avoid at all costs.

Difficult to understand. Always late and/or unprepared. Bad at answering questions. Doesnt respond to emails. Poor course structure. Aouar wasted so much time at the beginning of lectures, that she would race through the most important information (10-15 slides in about 30-45 seconds). GOOD LUCK
(list of negative feedback goes on)

analysis.name: Bruce Applegate
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed his lectures. He's funny and engaging and he really cares about us. My only complaint is that he is a bit scatter brained and his lectures were at times hard to follow. My main complaints aside from that have to do more with how the course is setup (3 grades, 2 professors, etc) and less to do with him specifically

Hardest class you will take at Purdue but Dr. Applegate is a great professor and is genuinely so funny. The first half of claaa is the other professor and all of the Midterms are completely written. This class basically covers every other class you have ever taken in high detail (genetics, BCHM, Orgo, etc) so STUDY A LOT….

You can tell Dr. Applegate is very knowledgable about the material he teaches (you would think this would go for all professors but you'd be surprised). It's obvious he loves what he does and it portrays during his lectures. He will go the extra step to help. He's also very funny! The class is difficult though since there are few chances for points

Its a shame he shares a class with 2 other sub-par professors. His section was by far the best. Engaging lectures and very easy to talk to outside class. He's a nice/funny guy who is obviously passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. The class is graded on 3 assignments (3 brutal(but fair)exams) which kind of sucked.

Solid professor and a really nice guy. His lectures are interesting, he adds lots of examples, and breaks down complicated topics. He's obviously very knowledgeable and willing to help students outside class whenever needed.

analysis.name: April Cheung
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Was not too bad, but the main issue is that she can be a bit harsh in terms of grading and ensures that the TA does the same. For example, there were many correct answers I have given, but the main issue is that she only marks it correct if we do it the way she prefers. Class was also fairly disorganized so that can have some improvement as well

She is very nice but she will not cut you much slack. Labs can be very difficult to complete if you do not finish them on time (it is a lab-heavy class). This class and ECET 227 are easily the hardest within the major.

Professor Cheung is a gem! She is easily accessed outside of class. If you do not finish a lab you are given the following week and can go into any of her other labs to finish! She is super nice and is great at explaining topics. Honestly, probably my top teacher in the ECET department.
Labs are hard but you'll do fine if you go to lecture and take notes.
She is one of the best professors at Purdue Polytechnic.

analysis.name: Aparajita Sagar
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I really liked the readings, and she was very nice; very helpful.  If you feel that being white and middle-class makes you feel left out, then it's only because of the subject matter, not because she tries to exclude anyone.  (So she teaches one of the required, "Be nice to women and minorities" classes - that's really not her fault).

Wonderful, caring, and facilitates so many important discussions about race, gender, class, and other issues that affect today. She has a great grip of history. She guides the discussions well. She chose some amazing books. And what's cool is that she is very open to new ideas and interpretations.

The vibes in Sagar's classroom are immaculate. If you show up having read the text, comment and think deeply about the experience of reading and expand on other ideas shared, she'll love having you in class just as much as you love having her as a professor. I'm used to being the one English nerd, but I don't feel like I'm alone in her class.

She will tell you that she gives pop quizzes, but she almost always announces them ahead of time. The papers are intense, but they are all relevant to what is discussed in class, which make them a lot easier to write. Professor Sagar was by far my kindest and favorite professor this semester, and I wish she could teach all of my classes.

I absolutely LOVED professor Sagar! She has been my favorite professor at Purdue yet. She is so sweet and caring, and the class is all discussion. She does give pop-reading quizzes, but if you read theyre easy! You also write lots of papers, but she makes expectations SUPER clear!! LOVE HER!! Take any course you can with her.

analysis.name: April Ginther
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This professor can be disorganized, but is incredibly intelligent, helpful, energetic about the material, and a joy to work with. Thanks to her, I worked twice as hard as other MA students I knew, but the final result was worth it. Thanks April!!

This class was very informative.  It had excellent coverage and a good pace.  I would recommend it for anyone who is interested in any type of language testing - including writing exams for your own classes.
She is a great mentor and supervisor. She's straightforward and offers good constructive comments all the time. I would highly recommend her as an adviser and teacher.

analysis.name: Konstantinos Ameranis
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Ameranis is goated! I found value in his lectures, and his style of teaching is very open and flexible. The accent was a bit hard to understand at times, but otherwise no complaints. Exams were tricky, but nicely curved. Do get started early on the projects tho. Also, his lectures on graphs & hashing were some of the best ive ever seen

He was a great professor even though it was his first time teaching the class. His lectures are engaging and he will ask the class questions throughout lecture. He is very accessible at his office hours and he was always very helpful at answering questions.
His lectures are engaging and he always motivates concepts before introducing them, which isn't that common in CS. He's also a really nice and approachable guy.

Professor Ameranis speaks clearly. Even though he is "new" at teaching, he gets to the point in lectures, he is not monotone or repetitive which makes the 50 minute lectures a breeze. If you have never programmed in your life, well lets just say you will need to put in a lot more effort than those kids who have been programming since 6th grade.

He's a new professor, but by no means unexperienced. I really enjoyed the setup of the lectures, as the concepts explained in class clicked very quickly apposed to if I had to miss a class and learn the information outside of class. 

Main thing: If you show up to classes, put in effort in class, and think critically you will do well.

analysis.name: Amanda Manning
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Amanda Manning is the best instructor I have had at Purdue. Her lectures are so straightforward, and her teaching style is amazing. She genuinely cared about each and every student and took the time to learn everyone's name. Office hours are helpful if you're ever struggling. If you can take her section, I highly recommend it!!

The attendance points dont really matter cause theyre 2/2, but if youre not good at math and dont go to class often you will be behind. The tests are 12 multiple choice worth 8 pts each so you gotta lock in. Make sure to do good on the first exam so you dont dig a hole for yourself right away (thats what I did). Also try not to cheat on homework.

Amanda Manning is an awesome teacher! It is obvious that she is passionate about everyone succeeding. Amanda truly cares about her students and also the class. I appreciated how well she taught the material; it was very easy to understand. At any point if you struggle or can't find your mistake on an assignment, go to office hours!

Amanda is so wonderful and full of energy even at 7:30 AM. If you have the chance definitely switch into her section. I hated math in high school but I actually felt like I understood it bc she explained it so well. She absolutely cares about her students success and I truly loved taking her class.

Seriously nice, and really focused on making learning more manageable for everyone. I learn really slow, and had previously failed the course with a different teacher, but I communicated my needs for a more personable environment, and she went above and beyond. Seriously, I should have bought her an Edible Arrangements for helping me pass the class

analysis.name: Andrea Kasinski
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 67 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I loved this class. The so-called “disrespect” was really Dr. Kasinski asking persistent talkers to quiet down so others could hear. When they didn't, she raised her voice and asked late students to use the back doors. I respect her for protecting those there to learn. If you truly want to learn cell biology, take this class.

I thoroughly enjoyed taking this course with Dr. Kasinski! She made the content interesting and easy to understand in lectures. Homework was challenging, but the three attempts were helpful. Exams were similar to past exams and accurately reflected what was covered in class and the notes she releases after class.

Amazing professor. Lecture content is clear and engaging, tests are easy and match the practice exams, and homework can be slightly challenging. For other reviews saying she is “disrespectful”: she got frustrated at the class after several instances of people talking over her up to 5 minutes into the lecture, which I think is reasonable.

She has help sessions every week and most of her exams are similar to practice exams. Homework has 3 attempts with 2 weeks dropped. Same for participation points, which is basically 100 points for attending class. She walks the class through processes to help with difficult concepts. Favourite bio class so far.

Makes a very complex curriculum extremely easy to learn, great lectures, and overall just a very easygoing and articulate professor. There's barely any homework but it's still great practice for exams, and exams are pretty easy especially with the practice exams she posts. Really easy class but still very interesting.

analysis.name: Amy Reibman
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof Reibman is a very nice professor. She may seem intimidating, but she cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed. Her homework can be tedious, but if you go to office hours, she will walk you through the problems. The exam averages are roughly in the 80's, and she usually targets them to be 75. Def recommend taking her classes.
Great command of the material. Exams weren't difficult at all if you understand the material. Best 302 Professor.

Lectures are average, lecture notes are very clear and nice to study from. Exams are fair in terms of content, but a big time crunch. Although I've mentioned some cons for Reibman, this is by far the professor you want for 301. She seems to care very much about students success and will accommodate new ideas/learning methods students suggest.

Overall very good, caring professor. Lectures could sometimes be a little scatterbrained/boring, but they felt like she actually cared about the content. Her homeworks were challenging, but interesting and actually fun to work on for the most part. Exams were very fair, high quality lecture notes posted online, etc. best 301 prof imo

Exams were HARD. They were long and each question was challenging. Lectures were fine, but having lecture late in the day was not ideal, especially since she speaks in monotone most of the time. Not a bad professor, but  there are better options out there.

analysis.name: Amanda Bies
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She was a great professor and really cares about what she teaches. She wants you to do well and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students. The text book is not really needed in my experience.
She's caring and passionate about what she's doing and has tone of experience
Lecture pretty much everyday but having the slides open would be useful. Also going to class helps with learning the material.

analysis.name: Amit Varma
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: My favorite professor ever. He was very clear during lectures and provided amazing notes. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but was very helpful to go in person.

Hes one of my favorite professors. Explains everything really well and does good examples. Cares about his students' success too! I had an early class with him so its hard to stay awake but its worth it! DONT SKIP!!

Professor Varma made me love learning again! I seriously wish every graduate level professor taught as clearly as him. Hard to beat his course content for Structural Stability; it's very well developed, as he's taught this course for a number of years. He does take a while to grade assignments, but he grades fairly. One of Purdue's best professors.
Excellent Professor. Explains everything in great detail. Don't sleep in his class. Very helpful and very intelligent. Always comes prepared, great examples, I highly recommend.
Awesome professor and all around great guy. He's really good at explaining difficult concepts and makes you want to come to class!

analysis.name: Amy David
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The assignment's grading rubric is extrme not clear, and the assignment always happened before lecture (you have to finish before learn the knowledge for this homework). When combine these two things, you will find even an AI will did better than you in the assignment. Also the professor will never tell why you lost your points in the feedback.

What a confusing class. Prof David was helpful during office hours but the entire semester-long project and lectures were super confusing from start to finish. She made video projects due the day after we get back from spring break. Communication was awful and grading system is weird, with everything pass-fail. Not hard, but strange - just be aware

There is no textbook. Lectures have very little content. Not much more than the powerpoint slides and sometimes the exercises/quizzes require you to know more than what the lectures teach. What was most annoying to me was the inconsistency in grading. Short answer questions would be scored 0% or 100%, even though the question was subjective

The farther away from her the better. I didn't learn anything from her. She only reads PowerPoint and does not give grades or standard answers until the end of the term. The mentor is fine. She didn't even check out our group's initial mistakes until our mentor checked them out before the final presentation.  she's ridiculous.

Do not take this class. I have been confused the whole semester. Her lectures are dry and not helpful. Very little content and wants you to do a project with Pepsico where she hands out  Word and Excel documents to do it all by yourself basically. Avoid this class. If this is required for your major, good luck.

analysis.name: Amy Marconnet
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Marconnet is a talented heat transfer professor. Her homeworks are long and at times tedious, but typically written in a way that leads students to the answers. Lectures are well-organized, although I would prefer if she leaned less on written-out equations presented rapid-fire and instead derived them herself at a more reasonable pace.

The class has an unreasonable amount of work and has some of the most challenging homework assignments I've experienced between both my undergraduate and graduate studies. The exams are similar to ME31500, but slightly less challenging. While most classes acknowledge that projects take time and effort, ME50500 doesn't slow down to accommodate.

Professor is a nice person, giving great lectures. There is no doubt you could learn real heat transfer, as well as some essential tools that engineers need. Unavoidably this is a difficult course, hws were super time-assuming, but exams were fair at most of the time. But no worry, she is generous but reasonable at final curve.

Prof. Marconnet seems to be pretty new to teaching. Tries to cram too much material into each lecture/week. Homework assignments were incredibly long. Added a group project to an already overbooked course. Responded well to emails, but was unforgiving and not understanding to conflicts and technical difficulties. Class was unnecessarily difficult.

She is a great lecturer, but tries to fit way too much material into an extremely short amount of time. The homeworks take forever. You will have no life if you take this class, burn out, and count yourself lucky to not have your wife divorce you by the end of it. Oh, there's a final project too. You *just* have to invent something completely new.

analysis.name: Amanda Veile
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: For a 3 credit class this was the easiest thing ever. Her lectures are very monotone and not the most engaging, but it was easy to zone out or do her homework during it and then get the attendance credit. There are no tests or quizzes, only online homework due every week. The labs were very interesting, and the whole class honestly felt fake.

This is probably the easiest class you can ever take in college. It is genuinely impossible to get below a 98 unless you just skip every class. No tests, exams, assignments are graded by participation, and on the homework you can answer as many questions as you want until you have a 100.

If you need to a UC science credit, I highly recommend you to take her ANTH 204. It's a free A. She gives out study guides before exams, and those study guides are basically the exam. Also, it doesn't even matter if you fail those exams because she provides tons of extra credit opportunities. I can feel her passion in her lecture. Amazing professor

overall not a bad class. lecture attendance is mandatory but the lectures tell you everything you need to know. most of the class is just inquisitives and the lab recitation. only thing that irks me is the way she says potentially.

She is so amazing!!! ANTH 204 was recommended to me because it is a science that is easy to follow, and it is great if you just need the credit. Dr. Veile makes it easy to get her students to achieve.

analysis.name: Steve Amireault
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

she does not care about this class at all. she frequently cancels classes and I'm 90% certain she doesn't even look at the assignments she grades. She brags about her industry experience despite the fact she's had very little and often teaches wrong information. She will not correct her mistakes

Dr Purpura is one of my favorite profs Purdue has. I had an incredibly difficult start to the semester and she sat down to make a study plan etc with me and genuinely cared. The grading in the ENGR classes is very strict though, so beware of that, but I recommend Sid as your prof.

Iqbal is a wonderful professor. He teaches great information on the basic things you will be doing as an engineer. Grading Criteria is clear but tough.

For Iqbal, in my experience, if you have any issues with your team members not completing assigned team work on time, do not expect any aid or help from Prof Iqbal.

One of the few ENGR132 professors who truly explains concepts well. If you pay attention in class, an A or A- is very achievable. Some exam questions came straight from slides he emphasized. I faced a course-related issue, and he was patient, helpful, and guided me through it.

Professor Iqbal was a wonderful class leader. His lessons can tend to run a bit long, but only because he specifies exactly what the course expects. If you listen, you shouldn't struggle very much. A great overall prof.  Can honestly say that I never came close to falling asleep in his class.  He is the only professor that I have ever had that will cuss at math.  Very entertaining and presents the material in a way that I found very helpful.

Dorsey is possibly the best prof I've had at Purdue! Wish I could have her again but I'm graduating! She makes the information interesting and is obviously an expert in her field! Armstong is one of my two favorite professors from my undergrad career. She's a GEM, both as a person and as a professor. She commands respect, but is kinda motherly towards her students. analysis.name: Arun Prakash
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Course is a lot of work, but taught well. Average week is: lectures, homework, quiz AND MATLAB project. There are 4 "Live Quizzes" during the semester that are essentially mini tests. I felt this class took time away from others to do well. Prof is always available and gives 2 attempts on hwks and quizzes. Review MATLAB and Lin Alg prior to course.

He is a good professor, but his teaching style really made things too complicated. Despite investing twice as much time as other courses into completing various assignments and quizzes, you may find that your grades do not reflect the effort you have put in. I think AAE 558 (FE Methods Aerospace Structures) is more helpful than this course.

This prof gives SO much work it is never ending. Definitely a class you have to stay engaged with or it's a steep hill to catch back up. Felt like grading was on a pendulum between very lenient and very strict. His lectures weren't the best but not terrible. Definitely needed the curve at the end. He is very accessible outside of class too.

Dr. Prakash takes a very rigorous approach to Statics. He explains in depth and assigns the most difficult problems. You really learn the material (and if not, you won't do too well...). He is exceptionally helpful, not only offering regular office hours but also in the semester I took the class, regular review sessions. Inspiring, great prof!

Prakash is approachable, kind, and explains topics thoroughly. If you have trouble deriving expressions symbolically, you may struggle in lectures, but he does lots of examples. HW is graded on effort, exams are hard but have lots of partial credit, and extra credit for attending lectures. Overall, would recommend Prakash.

analysis.name: Nelida Aubeneau
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Profa is one of my favorite professors at Purdue. She obviously cares for all of her students and will support your learning in her class. She is a fair grader and quick to respond to urgent emails. I would take any classes she teaches!

I loved Profe. Nelida! She was so kind, caring, and understanding of her students. Similarly, she provided great feedback on assignments and was inspirational/encouraging during her lectures. SPAN 301 underwent many changes, so she was extremely flexible with deadlines. I wish Nelida could be my Spanish professor for the rest of my time at Purdue!

profa nelida is the best professor i've ever had. she is so kind and remembers all of her students by name. she responds to emails fast and is very forgiving with deadlines. if you are taking any 300 level spanish, PICK HER AS YOUR PROF.
Extremely kind and understanding. Was not especially strict about deadlines, and was flexible when presented with a fair explanation for a missed/incorrect assignment.

Profa. Aubeneau was so kind and understanding. She helped me a lot when I didn't understand what was going on. She does teach the entire course in Spanish and she speaks a little fast, but it's very immersive. Exams are pretty hard but nothing you can't study for.

analysis.name: Audrey Ricke
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: There are a lot of complainers out there, but Ricke teaches her students to think critically about things. She is extremely intelligent in a broad range of subject areas.

Overall, a good professor. I enjoyed the class; there was a reasonable amount of work. As she explains in the beginning, the grade is made up of different categories, so if you aren't good at one thing, you can make it up with another.

Very impractical rules during her lectures. No laptops to take notes or anything like that. She whispers to a lecture hall of 200 students and expects everyone to hear her. Very convoluted lectures that jumped around and made little to no sense. Easy A, but I learned nothing. Complete waste of time.

Hands down, worst ANTH professor at Purdue. She is only focused on her research with German people in Brazil. Expects precise answers to vague questions. No computers allowed, and you'll lose points by having one. I'm an ANTH major and I had to retake this class with someone else, she was that bad. Glad she's only temporary.

Dr. Ricke's class was unnecessarily hard, honestly. Missing small amounts of points on reading exercises and tests could seriously hurt your grade, and she only has two tests (including the final). She offers very little review save for in-class oral lecture, and her powerpoints are super vague, and not very helpful.

analysis.name: Austin Cooper
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
Doesn't have any care for students.
Asks some questions in a perfunctory manner for the sake of asking.
Course has a lot of reading for a speech-related class.
Readings would never be read outside of class (boring, depressing). 
Grading rubric is nonspecific.
He literally can grade you according to his feeling that day or about you, which he does.

Very organized and has a sense of humor. However, he does not seem to be very caring about his students and can be a bit egotistical. One time I reached out with a suggestion and he laughed at what I said in a disrespectful way, even though I said something thoughtful. He also seems to grade based on his mood and how much he likes the student.

One of my favorite professors. Interesting lectures. Readings for class are really long but they're in place for homework. You don't have to do the readings to do well in the class. Definitely not an easy history class though requires some studying. Heavily based on writing assignments, but you don't have to be an excellent writer to excel.

So. Much. Reading.
For a class primarily for engineers / other STEM majors, Dr. Cooper does not hold back on the daily assigned readings. Between 40 - 80 pages of dense, confusing, BORING text. The pop quizzes are pretty tough. He basically expects you to understand/fully comprehend the text before its even discussed in class.

Dr. Cooper is very passionate about his field and teaches in an interactive way, making his lectures great. He answers questions well and is fair in evaluating student work. His History of the Nuclear Age course is well organized, but with only 6 assignments (including exams) and no curve, get ready to write some near perfect essays.

analysis.name: Ariel De La Fuente
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He only graded us out of 4 tests, but the tests were based almost 90% of his lecture. Only two questions in total were not covered in lecture.   He covers the readings during the lecture very well. His lectures are long and boring, but you can usually use him as an audio book and focus on something else.
Very interesting class. I really enjoyed the professor too. A few midterms and quizzes as well as an in person essay at the end. Highly recommend

Lectures can be a bit bland, it's just material but he does a good job of explaining content. I'd highly recommend going to lecture, there are no videos posted and it's easier than reading the slides from home. Read the textbook too!! I found that to be a great resource.
Absolutely despised this class. Do not take it if you have a choice! By far the worst class I have ver been in, professor sucks and so does the structure of the class

This professor changed the topic of the class throughout the semester. He eliminated about 1/3 of the books he listed as required by the end of the semester. The majority of the class ended up being about Argentina (I like Argentina but that was not how it was advertised). His lectures ramble and his quizzes & exams were unpredictable (mildly put).

analysis.name: Robert Austin
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Most of my gripes aren't actually because of the professor and his lectures but the class itself, and there's only so much he can actually do about that. There's a lot of homework and weekly quizzes that are harder than most midterms. He has fun demos he shows inside of class which make the class more interesting and help you learn.

Professor Austin may not be the best professor but overall he does a pretty good job. His lectures are not the best, but he tries to keep students engaged and explains the content well. Don't expect him to be too helpful outside of class, but compared to some other 172 professors he's a safer pick.

Many of the gripes I have with the course have nothing to do with Dr. Austin. Overall, he kept lectures interesting with demos + did the occasional unnecessary calculus derivation. If class taken w/ MA261 there is some overlap which is nice. Study Rubello's materials (especially the problem quiz videos and practic exams) + you will be fine.

I had him for ASTR 263 but RMP doesn't have that option. The lectures are pretty dull but the class is a free A. Two easy online quizzes, hard-to-fail slooh quests, and a gimmie final project. The outdoor night observations made this class and they were a good time. I'd still favor Andrew Freed's science credit instead.

There are pre lecture videos that you watch to have some understanding before class. He skips over these videos and the hard to understand material in them and teaches the easiest parts so there is lots of material he doesn't explain at all that will be on the tests. The course is not hard but he makes it hard because he doesn't explain material.

analysis.name: Benjamin Avery
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Avery is great! His feedback is direct, yet constructive, and despite the class being online, he was very accessible and easy to reach out to. He's very flexible with deadlines too; however, you don't want to exploit that, as it's very easy to fall behind in this class. Definitely recommend.

He was very good at responding to emails and answering questions. However, the way the course was set up through brightspace was a bit confusing. Overall, he was a good professor and was very quick to respond to questions.

Awesome class. Ben made a class i was terrified of fun. He is quite understanding but isn't afraid to call students out. Go to class and stay on his good side. His lecture about how to not screw up college was so rad. For sure take his classes if you have the chance

I would rate this class 3.5 on difficulty. Ben is very relatable and understanding, but don't skip his class and ask for favors he will roast you. If you don't participate you won't be on his good side, but he is an incredible teacher.

Ben was so funny, and we all had a wonderful time in his class. I learned more in his course than I have in any other course my first semester. He is very relatable, and has great content in his presentations. 10/10

analysis.name: Jordan  Awan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is overall a good professor and a pretty chill guy. I found the exams to ask a lot of curveball questions that were often buried *deep* in the lecture notes, resulting in some subpar exam scores. He's not the most passionate-seeming, but he does make sure that students understand the material taught in lecture and encourages participation.

Nice guy. Midterm was writing code by hand (not bad, I promise), and the final exam was purely conceptual (I took it today). Very clear grading criteria, which is really nice. The class is very "what you see is what you get" in terms of exam quality, so it's really easy to study for it. Not the type of guy to try and trick you with test questions.

Fantastic professor. All of the exam content is clearly covered in his lectures which are easily accessible and the labs are very helpful towards the learning in this course. Just start early on the projects and you will do great.

One of the best professors I have ever met at Purdue. The lectures are very well organized and he explains everything clearly. He also encourages class discussions before giving out solutions. I really learnt a lot and suggest taking this course with him. You won't regret it. The only issue I have is that lecture notes are not shared online.
Great professor! Puts in effort in his lectures and slides, and explains concepts well.

analysis.name: Avinash Kak
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 79 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Easily one of the best undergrad course professors at Purdue. 404 was such an entertaining and interesting class and I learned a lot during his lectures.

Unreasonable course load, does not account that students can have some things to do outside of this course. As a grad student, please do not take this unless you have no research, no other courses, and basically no life outside of this class. The course expects us to spend 1 week on the hws, which I do not understand in what world is reasonable!?

Least favorite ECE class. Professor goes over hundreds of pages of material in a lecture. Exams do not test understanding rather more about memorization. Need to use certain words in explanations or do not get points. Do not like how students are picked on in class for not understanding material. Not a constructive learning environment.

What we see here is the main problem with RMP. A single disgruntled student can post multiple negative reviews in order to exact revenge on a professor.  As is common with graduate classes, most of the students were foreign born and had no trouble with the professor -- except for this one student who got thrown out because he was mostly absent.

I was in class and I feel this issue could have become much serious. Imagine being forced to drop a class 3 weeks before semester end-> failing to meet visa credit requirement->losing student visa status or getting an unfair F-> failing to graduate on time-> losing job offer. I wouldn't recommend any of his classes to international students.

analysis.name: Ayman Habib
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: There is no direction in this course. His lectures put half the class to sleep because he looks at the class twice during the hour the lecture because he talks to the white board. Nobody has any clue what is expected or what we are learing. 1/10 would not recommend.

Very hard to understand and very boring. Habib is a poor lecturer that gives way too much information. The labs and tests were ridiculously hard and labs took 10 plus hours a week. the tests were difficult to study for. the textbook was very expensive and almost never used. absolutely awful teacher teaching a pointless class. 0/10 change majors.

Habib is an incredibly awful lecturer. He expects students to pick up on material immediately and then criticizes you if you don't. He's one of those that makes a huge deal about phones, but can't keep anyone's interest for 2 minutes. Labs are beyond awful. Worst professor I've had at Purdue.

Habib is a very boring lecturer. He covers an huge amount of information in lecture and it is unclear on what is actually important or not. Provides no useful study materials so students have no idea what to expect on the test. Also, weekly labs take at least 8 hours to complete.

No textbook. Must attend lectures to view new material. Doesn't post class notes online for weeks at a time because he prioritizes punishing students over teaching them. Progresses quickly. Combo'd with  TA's who seemingly have never taught before, resulting in a marathon of pain. Not fun at all.

analysis.name: Ayhan Irfanoglu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Irfanoglu is about the best professor you can get for Dynamics. Class is very exam-heavy (75% of grade) but exams were very similar to homework problems and gracious with partial credit. Unlimited attempts for weekly quizzes. Lectures are somewhat boring, consisting mostly of working through practice problems, not a much on the theory behind them.

He loves teaching and you can tell it from day one. Brings amusing toys to class to explain physics which usually helps. He sometimes gets so engrossed in teaching that he forgets that he is teaching a class and seems almost mumbling but if your frequency matches with his, you will learn a lot. If not, god save you !!!
He is such an intelligent professor to study under, and I would take his classes anytime. He really cares the ones who put hard work.

Cons  Homework is due at the first minute of class. If you're late even by just five minutes he won't take it. Will call out people who aren't paying attention or look at their phones and say things like you should drop this class occasionally.  Pros  As long as you attempt the homework, you get full points.  Still better than Haikal trust me.
He thinks in his head when he does the problem and doesn't write down all the procedures.  So I'm usually confused in class.

analysis.name: Ayan Maiti
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Nice professor, and very knowledgeable. Helps his students to appreciate the beauty of mathematics. Most bad ratings are from the kids who need all their problems solved on a plate they can memorize to get an A. If one simply does his exam review problems there is no reason one would not score well. Take him, if u don't need spoonfeeding.

Took the class asynchronously over summer. It was pretty chill. The lectures were neat, but you could easily self-study and get a pretty good score on the homework and the exams, which is what I did. I do wish the homeworks had partial credit though.

Professor Maiti is a great lecturer and is very knowledgeable on the material and its applications outside of the classroom. He cares very much about  his students performance and makes an extra effort to make sure his students understand the material. Definitely recommend this professor.

His homework was not as tough as some professors but the lectures got rather hard to follow. This class is inherently hard but he talks really fast and doesn't exactly explain things the best which makes it a bit harder. His exams are fair but not really similar to practice exams. Just do a lot of practice problems and understand all the topics.

Avoid solving practice problems before exams.
Will not provide solutions to practice problems.
When asked, only drop hints instead of solving problems for students.
Rarely respond to students' emails.
Disappear when we show up to his office hours.
Pick the hardest homework assignments for students. 
Expect students to memorize everything for exams.

analysis.name: Ariel Azar
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Azar was a really caring knowledgeable prof, let people speak & really listened also saying its important to have contrasting views bc that's how academics learn and grow, talks about race well. Class was organized a little weirdly, but prob bc he cares to cover all the topics and also taught it the first time this sem. No bio hw like other SOC310

It is an advanced level gen-ed class I have to take for my ECE diploma. From this perspective, despite I do not fully agree with the concepts taught in this class, it is desirable - professor is kind and respectful; course materials are very easy. Attend the lectures and agree with what they teach (or pretend you do) then it is an easy A.

His lectures were sometimes boring and the assignments a bit tedious, but he was understanding and laid-back. I didn't find him strict or a tough grader. It seems like the other reviewer might have been offended by the course materials because the AI graphs weren't a major part of the course, and keeping up with quizzes helps.

I think this was the professors first time teaching this course and it showed. Grading was never updated on timely manner. Final exam without any sort of study guide/topics list. Attendance is mandatory and answering discussion questions in class was a big part of the grade.

analysis.name: Kamyar Azizzadenesheli
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Everything for the class was taken from a Standford online course. As a result, the homeworks were of very high quality. Lectures were decent. The exams were fully online and way too easy to find the answers on the internet so no one learned as much as they should have.

He is a really heartless person. very rude and shrew. brags about his research and his mentor all the time. doesn't consider students' time worthy of anything. I got a good grade in his course but this guy has a very sadistic and taunting nature. beware
Lectures are really boring and I struggle to stay awake. He gives Stanford courses' homework without giving the same quality of lectures. Homework is quite long too.

Lectures are almost entirely useless. Very boring and doesn't go over how to actually solve problems that are on the homework. But he uses all of Stanford CS 221's homework, so it is super easy to cheat. I've learned absolutely nothing from this class and will probably get an A still. I like his personality, but omg this class was terrible.

analysis.name: Ayhan Ince
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class is awesome. It is  very challenging but very applicable. Prof. Ince does a very good job at relating the class to the real world and it makes the class more enjoyable.
Professor Ince is a great professor and his MET214 class is one of the best taught classes I have taken at Purdue. He is by far one of the best professors I've had.

Great Professor. Actually wants to challenge you. If you pay attention, go to lecture, and study, you will do well. If you think that a good professor is one that allows an easy A, then this class will be challenging. He is probably the smartest prof. I have had here which is something to respect. You can learn a lot form him if you put in effort.

Very knowledgeable and smart prof. You can get very high grade if you show that you really understand  important course topics and explain well your work and include all your assumptions in the paper. Even if there are numerical errors in your calculations and your numbers aren't quite right.

Professor Ince really knows what he is talking about. One of the smartest professors I have had. Always could answer any question. He wants students to learn and creates life stories to explain what is important in the workplace. This has been my favorite class to date, but also the hardest.

analysis.name: Phillip Baeza
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: MGMT 245, he spends his lectures talking about what seems like everything but excel and on certain assignments he told us "I told my TAs to not help on this homework" which leaves you without a support system sometimes. He also took pride in making the class very hard until the first exam average was a 60%.Its a freshman level class not a 500 level

I had him for MGMT245 but it wasn't an option. Baeza is pretty chill, however I do think a lot of us struggled in the class because this course is basically CS-type hard (im not cs tho so dont @ me) but we were lowkey expecting it to be a basic excel course. the first unit is easy but it advances FAST. make sure u pay attention in lectures. lock in

Phillip is horrible. He reads off the slides like a middle schooler doing a presentation for the first time and proceeds to take points off on your project if you do the same. He also goes on random tangents and doesn't teach almost any relevant material to the exams or homework which makes exams extremely difficult. This class is a waste of time.

He is a great professor. He checks all the boxes. He cares about his students and has very reasonable expectations.  This is the most well-thought-out class and probably the best-taught class I have taken at Purdue. The only drawback is that the material leans towards the boring side, but the guest lecturers and prof B's enthusiasm make up for it.
Philip is outstanding. Nice dude, best prof I've ever had. Anyone would be lucky to have him as a teacher.

analysis.name: Papia Bawa
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took her On-line class at Ivy-tech. It's the worst class I've ever taken. Useless PowerPoints, No commends for drafts and stupid grading. For an assignment I worked for several days, only because I submitted one or two minutes late, she didn't even read it and just give me an zero. I learned nothing from her, change your section if you got her.
She's too opinioniated when grading, doesn't grade fair.

Has very unrealistic expectations for an 8 week course. Her grading and comments almost seem AI generated. She dances around what you actually need to work on and truly grades too harshly for an entry level english class.

Have Technical Writing online. Have never received the poor discussion board grades before. With this class, I have yet to have a good grade on them. Points are taken away, yet never told what was wrong with the posts or assignments. If I don't know what is wrong, how can I be learning? Can't correct mistakes if I don't know what the mistakes are.

Makes the semester a drag. Compared my workload with others taking ENGL 420 and it was ridiculous! Don't expect to get very much credit for your work. She will take points like crazy! Always talks about being concise, but I never completely understand what's going on. Switch sections and get someone else!

analysis.name: Dean Ballotti
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: A really nice professor, many assignments and projects, attendance is needed, but everything is not too hard if you love geography, only need you to pay attention, lectures are interesting, just like telling stories, there also have some funny short talks, you will never feel boring, he loves his students and always smile to them, like a old friend

Extremely fun professor. He's passionate about the subject, engaging in lectures, encourages genuine discussion, explains the material thoroughly and meaningfully, and clearly cares about his students. Assignments were all narrative based, requiring you take a position and write about it in discussion posts and quizzes. Great class and an easy A.

I took EAPS375 with professor Ballotti this semester and overall its been great, the lecture slides are very good and the professor talks at a good pace, information that we need to know was covered well. Quizzes are what took up about half of the course's grade and you have to answer them thoroughly to do well. Overall good experience.

There's a lot of content, but slides are always posted for review and the topics given are interesting. You learn not only about fossil fuels themselves and how they work, but also history behind them and how our society revolves around them. Teacher is very kind and courteous.
Prof. Ballotti is very passionate, very knowledgeable, and very engaging as a professor. I got more out of his class than I thought I would. Would love to take more classes with him.

analysis.name: Rachel Bailey
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof Bailey is not as bad as these reviews say, but still not easy. She was nice to both me and my groups in emails. The worst part of the class is that she is pretty harsh grading the big group projects, so be sure to do well on the other things to try and offset that. Read the instructions well because she WILL deduct for the smallest things.

If you can please DON'T take this class! This class requires tons of work, random small points are taken off, and the professor sends an insane amount of announcements. Aside from one useful project, the majority of the assignments were busywork and seemed inconsiderate of students' overall workload.

One of the most uncaring professors I've had so far at Purdue. There is SO much busywork that really doesn't aid your learning at all, it's more reasons for her to find something small and particular to deduct points from. Avoid.

Honestly it was nowhere near as bad as the other reviews have said. As long as you write something competent that hits the word count you'll get a perfect on individual assignments. She also grades within 24 hours and is one of the only professors I've had that gives personalized feedback for every single assignment.

I was scared of taking this class with her because of the ratings but she was awesome. My group had a problem with the company we were supposed to work with and she understood everything. I emailed her often to ask her some doubts I had and she responded quickly. Just try to send emails to her in a professional way and you will be fine.

analysis.name: Hayden Barber
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Barber is one of my favorite professors. His class is very interest-based and open to further exploration. I contracted his class for honors credits, and he was very knowledgeable, enthusiastic, and easy to work with. If you like to be involved, you'll love his class!

Dr. Barber is a decent professor. However, his class DOES NOT need to be an hour and fifteen minutes long. The class itself is fine, pretty boring but not hard. The class consists of mainly papers. He takes a while to get back to you on assignment drafts and isn't very good at communication, which is weird as he is a communications teacher.

Professor Barber was great! He was really easy to talk to if you needed help catching up on things. He is younger so he understands what it's like to be a student and how the stress can become overwhelming. Super accommodating and I would definitely take a class of his again!

Awesome professor! Longer lectures but he keeps them interesting and tries to get people to participate. He is passionate about what he teaches and was helpful when I fell behind and gave me all the time I needed to catch up. Will go out of his way to help students understand the content. Recommend taking any class that he's teaching!

Dr. Barber was an outstanding professor. He was enjoyable to listen to and talk to outside of class. He is intelligent and seems to care about his students. Sometimes I can get lost when lecturing because his lectures can be disorganized, but he does a good job of getting the class engaged.

analysis.name: Ekaterina Babintseva
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I would select other tags if I could. There is not a bad thing I could say about this Professor other than the fact I can only take this class once with her. She is incredibly caring about her students, listens to everyone, and actually makes a very caring class environment. I felt like some of my happiest memories were made in that class.

I had Babintseva for SCLA 102 and she was absolutely wonderful! She tried her best to make the reading engaging and seems to actually value student feedback. She was a very complimentary grader, as well. Most of the class was reading outside of class with discussions in class, and there were many extra credit opportunities. Highly recommend her!

Very kind and inspiring professor, you can tell she cares a lot about her students and the class! She makes a great effort to stimulate class discussion and weighs in with her own points, which were always insightful and often very funny. The books for SCLA 102 were overall good, and the theme of the class (Fall 25) was amazing.

She is absolutely phenomenal. Class was a good mix of lecture and group discussion. She has genuine respect for her students' input and intellect, and she is so kind. It is not an easy class, there's a lot of reading, but I found it to be rewarding and interesting.

She's an amazing professor and really knows a lot about the subject matter. Whenever she was speaking people would be really invested because she provided a lot of insight that we wouldn't have figured out on our own. In general she's super nice and tends to laugh during our lectures which keeps them lighthearted and fun. Just super awesome.

analysis.name: Becky Bokrand
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She gives amazing bullet points on what to study for exams. The lectures are super boring, but that is more so accounting than her. Dr. Bokrand is super kind and passionate about what she does. She gives great resources to succeed, and extra credit here and there. The class is an easy GPA booster, even if you have trouble staying awake.

I took Dr. Bokrand's accounting class and thought she was a good professor. Some material was confusing at first, but her explanations and review days helped a lot. Homework was challenging but useful, and exams reflected what she reviewed.

He is **** too, so choose a American teammate.

He is the worst professor I have had in all my four years hear at Purdue. That pretty much sums it up. I've been in the class for over two months now and haven't learned a thing. Literally the worst professor I have ever had at purdue. Reads off pdfs for lectures without clear guidance on anything.

At first taking his class I wanted to die however you get used to him. He loves to hear himself talk so a lot of his classes don't end up how he plans them because he often gets sidetracked. He has valuable feedback it's just hard to listen because he loves rambling. I have so much more I could say, prepare for some yoga!
Petronio is so fun! He talks like strongbad and is just as cool! Also very helpful outside of class and ready to help!

analysis.name: Michael Bergmann

review_highlights.comment: Likes to hear himself talk. For a subject as interesting as Philosophy, he made it one of the most dull experiences of my life. Paired with a no devices policy, the lectures are just him reading from the text and going on and on, not answering questions well, never ready to concede a student is right. Fair exams with good preperation material.

Utter lack of empathy for students who have the misfortune of attending his class. While he's passionate about the subject matter that he covers for this class, the way he pushes it down your throat is not nice. Most students are here simply for credit, don't make the class unbearably difficult. Makes you print your work AND expect you to write it.

I am in PHIL223 and have taken 3 phil classes before this. Professor Bergmann is meticulous and I understand none of his lectures. He explains things terribly and expects us to understand topics before we learn. he considers our hw study guides but DOESNT GIVE FEEDBACK UNTIL AFTER WE TAKE THE TEST. I have never hated a class more in my life.

A really great professor who knows his stuff about religion! Reading the book isn't really necessary as he goes over everything in excruciating detail. He has his overhead notes up online and exams should be a snap if you put effort into filling out the study guide. Definitely recommended for anyone interested in religion.

I was very excited to take the theory of knowledge but sadly the professor has a clear bias against people who are skeptics. Essentially what Bergman teaches is what Satre would consider bad faith. Definitely not an open ended class and unless you are into epistemology this class probably will not be fun for you.

analysis.name: Beatriz Galarza Tohen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the most caring profs I've had at Purdue. I remember near the end of the semester she told me that my smile genuinely brightened her day. Said at the beginning of the semester that she would always take our side no matter what. Genuine unconditional kindness that you don't see often elsewhere (but should).

ENGR 131 isn't a hard class. It's not too exciting either, but Prof. Galarza did her best to make classes kinda fun or have us practice an engineering soft skill (teamwork). 
Prof. Galarza is one of the nicest, most caring professors at Purdue. She also bumped my A- up to an A because I asked (the FYE 3.2 GPA, iykyk), because I got to know her.

She might be one of the most caring professors at this university. She's always available for her students and she truly wants you to succeed. ENGR 131 wasn't a hard class but I had a 7:30, and I'm really thankful that I had her class because I didn't often dread getting up to go to it. She also gives you a lot of studio time to work on projects.

ENGR 13100 I think is a pretty tedious class because the course fits a lot into a few months. Dr. Galarza made the class so much more tolerable. She is a sweet and supportive teacher and is the first person at Purdue who made me feel like I belonged. She makes effort to know all of her students personally and really cares about their well-being.

Professor Galarza is super caring and always makes sure to asks students how they are doing. She is also very helpful when answering students' questions. The class curriculum itself is slow and tedious though so I would recommend taking ENGR 133 over ENGR 131 if you're taking a lighter course load.

Dr. Bitt was by far my favorite professor, I suggest that you actually get to know him because he is a great guy and wants all his students to succeed. I recommend this class for literally anyone it amazing and not hard at all.
One of the Best professor I ever met.

analysis.name: Bettina Klose

Guessing that most of the reviews are from an earlier period. The exams were difficult, but we were told what to study. This course was more difficult than most but not the hardest I have ever taken.

Poorly designed course. She lets the curve do all the work. You will pass the class as long as you aren't the very bottom. Her grading is the most unreasonable and inconsistent I've ever seen out of all my years of undergrad, graduate and even high school. This is the first and only time I've cried because of class. Avoid at all costs if possible.

Bad lectures, I would ask for help with something, and she seemingly wouldn't read the full question before responding with a nonhelpful answer. Prepare to teach yourself. Dr. Klose is lecture-heavy. Her entire class is composed of going over material in a pretty bland way. She's unclear on how much work to show during problem sets and exams. Exams are pretty tight on time.

analysis.name: Ilias Bilionis
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
