review_highlights.comment: Prof. Bilionis is by far one of the best professors I have had while at Purdue. He gets that the homework might make you solve it the long/hard/stupid way, but he always (eventually) takes the time to show you the shortcuts so that during the exam you can quickly answer problems. Prepares us well for the exams (2nd highest section average).

Great prof, ME539 is graded solely based on homeworks and is very interesting. I really appreciate that he used real data in assignments. ME697 is a different beast - if you are thinking of taking it after ME539 just consider the workload  nad difficulty of content.

My best professor this semester. Very engaging, excellent knowledge of material and even better at communicating it to the class. He finds a way to make the class fun, while still keeping control over the students. ME 270 is a class which will require more homework than you might expect, but, upon completion, exams will be a breeze.

Grade was based entirely on homework. Grading was very lenient. Lots of partial credit for effort. And he provides a lot of code to help you. This class is much easier compared to Numerical Methods. He really loves proofs…which weren't very useful for homework, and so lectures weren't too helpful.

He is a good lecturer, funny, and keeps the class interested. Loved his attitude. Would recommend him for this course. Text is never used to read but has all the homework in it. Prepare to have homework every class.

analysis.name: Stephan  Biller
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining

Would take another class with Professor Biller, 10/10.

One of the greatest professors teaching at Purdue. Has an incredible amount of industry experience which he infuses into the course. Teaches the content extremely well, is funny and caring. Assignments are challenging but fare but the grading structure is generous. This simulation portion is a lot of fun. One of the best IE courses!

Easily one of the best and most important classes you can take. Class setting focus on real world cases of digital transformation, reviewing cases and technologies, industry speakers who are leaders in their field, interesting labs and is taught by one of the best professors in the university. Class has a decent amount of work, highly recommend!

Digital Transformation in Industrial Business with Professor Biller is enlightening, with case studies on various companies that give us insights on real-world implementations. There are group presentations on cases and technologies. The use of technologies like @Risk, working in labs, and guest lectures are like the icing on the cake.

Best class I have taken till date: IE5900 Digital Transformation in Industrial Business.

Unique class offerings:
1. Case Study discussions
2. Team based work
3. Covered various spectrums of Industry 4.0
4. Leveraged top-notch scale-at-lab, Purdue's Lambertus 
5. Real-time examples drawn-in for learning
6. Guest speakers invited
7. @Risk tool used

Proffessor Bickle is a really smart and seems like a nice guy. Biggest complaint with the class was that the material covered in class was always extremely easy compared to the sorts of questions on the homework and especially the exams. Learning outside of class will probably be necessary.

Very monotnous lectures. It's very clear he knows what hs is doing and he is very smart, the lectures were just very hard to follow. He told me I should drop the class because he didn't think I would be able to get the grade i needed on the final

Thanks to her I spent my lovely fall break writing lab reports!

Suchly a lovely lady :))

(20%) Overall not bad

Good professor, known mostly for his wine appreciation class. Concentrated too much on the history and background of different wine regions, a lot of theory. Did not teach how to identify flavours or aromas during actual tasting. Still a great course, helpful in real life.

analysis.name: Alan Bunning

Great lecturer but you have to keep with the work to be successful.

Bunning always had good informative lectures that were easy to follow and take notes. However, the CS159 course is terribly designed which is not Bunning's fault. Group labs were terrible as one person ended up doing most of the work and the grading on the your code being efficient rather than working was not cool. If the code works its works.

Does iClicker questions at the beginning of lecture for attendance. Answering them at all is sufficient. Don't talk too loudly during lecture or he'll call you out. Don't share homework code with one another, they catch it easily. His notes cover almost all the material; I'd say the book is redundant. Exams are tough - know your concepts and terms.

Professor Bunning was fantastic at explaining the C language. His way of teaching made learning more complex topics easier to grasp. While his lectures aren't the most engaging in the world, they are very informative and critical if you want to do well in this class. Overall, this course is overly hated and isn't too bad in reality.

analysis.name: Heejung Byun

I switched into a 7:30 section to have Professor Byun. Never regretted it. He is super kind, very knowledgeable, and overall one of my favorite business professors. The class consisted mainly of a few short writings (1 paragraph max), some case study analyses, a midterm, final project, and final exam. AI is encouraged on the final project. 10/10!

Lectures were very interesting and easy to follow-he really cares about what we are learning about. There are case studies, so there is a decent amount of reading, but the cases are easy to be interested in & he's not harsh on grading. His midterm was difficult imo, but the average wasn't bad. Final project is not difficult, AI is encouraged!

Taking this class with Professor Byun was one of the most fun experiences I had at Purdue! The class was very interesting to be in and he was very well prepared for each class. Highly recommend this class and this professor. Wish there are more professor's like him out there who are out to be a good person and inspirational teacher!

Worst professor I have ever had. Often times goes on tangents about random things that have nothing to do about the class topic. Heard from some people to not take this professor, and to drop the class, wishing I did. I leave this class every lecture wishing I had never taken the class. Very poorly run class, grades are based upon 3 essays.

One-credit course with quizzes based on the textbook and more. Independent studying was required, as not all quiz material was reviewed in class. Really strict grader, and way too much work for one-credit.

Sexuality and Family Life with Dr. Elias is a great class. It is a mix of traditional lectures and guest speakers. The tests are very straight forward. Super nice professor and really fair grader. Attendance really matters in this class but I plan to take her classes again in the future.

Teach a class vs. basking the spotlight/attention.

analysis.name: Charles Campbell
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I have taken multiple classes with him, and from those I have figured out, he is a very unorganized professor. Moving around exams last minute, giving the wrong amount of time for test, not grading the homework, along with changing the syllabus or not providing one to follow. He has made many students drop out and retake under another professor.

He gives little to no feedback and when he does he phrases things extremely vaguely and to the point where you have no clue what he's actually saying. A lot of reading is needed. his organization skills are bad to say the least we had a full schedule planned only lasted 4 weeks. There are pop quizzes throughout the class that are you can't makeup.

For a written communication course, it was harder than it had to be. Late graded assignments, not following the syllabus schedule, vague assignment descriptions, vague and unclear communication, one-size-fits-all teaching style, condescending attitude, and a few, if any, applicable constructive feedback on essays and written assignments.

Initially a very tough professor but he gets nicer over time. Makes you really work for your grade on the essays but is easy with other assignments. He's very intimidating but not a bad teacher. He provided a lot of guidance for the final essay but the first one was basically us going in blind. Not impossible to get a good grade though.

Not as bad as described, but expect late grading and unclear information on your grade, and surprise mini-quizzes that will contribute to a significant portion of said grade. If you actually do the reading and come to class on time, you'll do fine. Stress on the time bit since the quizzes are usually done in the first 2 minutes.

analysis.name: Kubilay Cirik
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Kubilay is very knowledgeable and genuinely wants to ensure we learn the concepts well. He is always available for help.
Great professor who is always available for help, always relates course materials to the real business world..
Good professor, always ready to help ..

Professor Cirik is a good professor, his class just needs restructuring. It is on zoom and he reads straight from the PowerPoint until the last minute. However, he's nice and responds to emails quickly. If this class was in person, it would be great. You do only have test and project grades, so there is no homework grade cushion.

I had him at LSU and his lectures were pretty boring. He gave extra credit if you came to class, but attendance was not mandatory (though he did give credit for participation). The tests were mostly test bank, and the group project is on an article chosen by him and it was fairly easy. Not a hard class, but also not very fun.

analysis.name: Vernon Cisney
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This is my 5th course with Professor Cisney, and I have enjoyed all of them enormously. Throughout my time on campus, I have yet to take a class with a more caring, genuine, and down-to-earth professor than him. He is noticeably passionate about the subjects he teaches, and will help you if you reach out to him seeking guidance on an assignment.

His Philosophy in Film FYS was one of my favorite classes at Gettysburg. His lectures are the best! He splits class time between lecturing on important background information and cultivating engaging discussions with his students. He also truly cares for his class.  He is clear in what he expects on papers, and I found him to be a fair grader.

one of the best profs i had because he was so easy and friendly. his tests are easy and as long as you show up to class and pay attention he'll really help you understand what you need to know. likes to get to know his students and is really easy to talk to for help. make sure to put a little effort in and you'll really enjoy the class.

Make sure you go to lecture, even though he posts outlines online. He's an entertaining lecturer and really does his best to help everyone understand  the material. His exams are really easy if you just look over the study guide and ask questions about it before the exam. This was truly a fun class.

Cares a lot about his classes, very helpful for the most part if you go to his office hours. Hw is just keeping up on reading and the lectures in class are very important because he will go over things

analysis.name: Mark Cipolla
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He tries, but the voice... oh my God the voice.
Unfortunately you have to take the course...

analysis.name: Raymond Cipra
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: gives a ton of work and expects more from students than what they can give. No clear grading criteria. can give very dry boring lectures that are hard to follow. Close to useless in office hours because he explains it the same way again and again and gets frustrated when you don't understand.
Tough grader for no reason. Exams and labs aren't returned until the end of the semester. Exams don't test your knowledge of the subject only tests your ability to remember phrases from the book.

Prof Cipra tries to be funny in the class with some outdated jokes. He expects something which he never conveys clearly. Very strict marking and the papers are very low on standard of engineering. He expects you to read some weird readings and you end up losing marks on the silliest of questions. Manages to screw up a v imp design course. VVPOOR.

Not only is professor Cipra terrible and explaining the material he needs to, he refuses to review material that is crucial for learning.  He will call everything (even brand new material) 'trivial' and will refuse to do examples.  Exams in this class are not about how well you can work through the material, but if you can see the subtle trick.

Expected much more from this class. Ended up with exams which put an emphasis on study by heart and memorization book content and million bullet points. I found it very hard to memorize so many useless words   from the textbook. He made fun of something from my part of the world during my 1st semester in the U.S. Made me feel so unwelcome.

analysis.name: Claire Mason
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Mason does a great job of giving her students creative freedom throughout the semester! Often times you forget you are working because you have a lot of room to have fun with the projects. BE AWARE that there is more to the syllabus assignment than you may think... overall amazing professor though!

SCLA 101 was my least favorite class of my first semester of FYE. This is because of Professor Mason. She did not teach me a singular thing the entire semester. She throws assignments at you that are massive amounts of your grade and just expect you to do well on your own. Her class left me dreading each time I had to see her. Avoid at all costs.

Amazing professor! With Mason, SCLA 101 quickly became my fav class of the week. She is incredibly sweet, will remember your name since the first day of class and gives great feedback. Be aware, however, that she is a strict grader, so if you try to do your work last minute you will be done for.

For a mandatory class for some majors, it was honestly fun. Professor Mason makes you think about things from an entirely new perspective, which I was surprised by. Also, DO NOT PULL UR PHONE OUT IN CLASS. SHE WILL MARK YOU ABSENT. BELIEVE ME SHE CAN SEE WHEN UR PHONE IS OUT. YOU CAN NOT HIDE IT.

You can tell she truly cares about her students and teaching. Her class is really engaging and she gives us plenty of time for assigments. I never like English classes but she made this one really fun, would definitely recomend taking her for SCLA101 if you can.

analysis.name: Clinton Chapple
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Chapple was a good lecturer, and was very passionate about the topic. Homeworks and exams depended heavily on lecture content. Even as a non-bchm major I found the class interesting and easy.

Dr. Chapple is an amazing professor who is truly dedicated to helping his students become interested in biochemistry. He teaches BCHM100 through a series of case studies which makes the concepts easy to understand. The homework is hard, but manageable. Exams are very concept and application based.

Dr. Chapple is an incredible professor.  I thought the course was very doable.  It does require studying.  There were only 4 or 5 quizzes and they were not bad at all.  Homework is graded harshly, but that just depends on the TA.  I really enjoyed this class, but I am a biochemistry major, so I could see how others would think it was challenging.

This is definitely not a 100 level class. Prof is great & you learn a lot of useful stuff but extremely difficult. I've been getting A+ on all of the assignments, and pretty sure I was one of the top students in class but did bad on just one final and I got a C. quizzes&hw easy, exams are ridiculously hard. its ridiculous. def not 100 level

I had Dr.Chapple for his last time teaching BCHM100. He is a nice professor but overall it seemed like he was lazy in helping students. The course material was hard to understand and the homework grading is brutal unless you go to see a TA for 'help'. Basically he just wants you to know what a protein looks like and if you can draw it.

analysis.name: Rosalie Clawson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Clawson not only gave out an amazing online class, but she was kind and accessible by email at all times. I really enjoyed the content - especially the discussion of feminism and how it has advanced over time. Overall, a great online class if you need a civics requirement/POL credit!

Prof Clawson wasn't exceptional, but not terrible either. The exams are closed book, while quizzes are open book. There are multiple articles, papers, videos, etc. that need to be read/watched weekly. That part of it was annoying, and I felt most weren't even helpful. There are no extra assignments, so you're just graded on tests/discussions.

This class was interesting and super easy. Only assignment each week is a discussion board and a peer response. There are quite a few of supplemental readings that need to be done each week as you are tested on them, but quizzes and exams are pretty easy otherwise. Great class to take for civics literacy or other requirements.

The online class is one of the easiest things I have ever done. It is 1 discussion board post with 1 response per week. The reading (although mandatory) does not really matter unless you are taking a test.

For an online class, it's a bit difficult to get a full picture of a professor, but Clawson does well at making herself available, while simultaneously maintaining a level of professionalism and care for her study and students, especially during COVID. The subject matter is interesting, and you will read some of her own publications in the course.

analysis.name: Tracy Clark
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Most boring class you could take. Easy class just take it with any other teacher. Lectures are pointless and monotone. She is obsessed with blogging.

Tracy Clark, while well-intentioned, is a subpar professor whose course and material did not teach me about--nor reflect principles of--technical writing. Her Brightspace is bloated, with redundant class assignments taking longer to explain than complete. You can do well, but sitting through her mandatory lectures is tiring. Go online if you can.

Tracy's Brightspace setup is confusing; assignments are giant text blocks that require multiple tabs to decode. Lectures are long with little substance—she once spent 5+ mins explaining how to click a button. Attendance is strict; missing over three classes drops your grade by multiple letter grades even with perfect HW grades. Avoid this class.

like everyone else said, she talks *so much* without conveying much of substance. she attempts to make her BrightSpace navigable and fails since her attempts at clarity result in an overwhelming amount of information. the course is easy, the grading's light, the late "policy" is laughable, and she makes you do things in class that never get graded.

Tracy is like a disorganized teenager. She is exceedingly passive aggressive, talks excessively without saying anything of substance, and bends her own rules when its to her own convenience. 

Given her role as an English teacher, I am surprised by her lack of proficiency in the writing. Purdue should discontinue her employment. Advice? Avoid her.

analysis.name: Clifford Fisher
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Genuinely cares for the learning of students with a mix of good humor and clear communication. You read textbook / watch lecture videos before class then discuss the material in class. There are short quizzes at the start of class to check if you read/watched the material. Would 100% recommended taking with Fisher.

I really enjoyed my time in Cliff's MGMT 254 class. I would definitely recommend taking MGMT 254 with Cliff, as you learn so much in a fun way. Tests are 80% of your grade, and they are online, and 20% is participation, which is just going to class and doing the "project" in the first 5 minutes of class.
He is very careless about those students who struggle in his class. He does not provide any study material for the exams!!! He is a good person but not as a professor!

Great guy. 80% of MGMT254 was exams and the other 20% was attendance. He will pick on you in class if you don't have your name tag up. If you're on his good side, he leaves you alone and enjoys asking you for help when doing class assignments. I got an average of 67% on all exams but the curves are GIANT because many people fail. Great guy overall.

Cliff is a great professor and is very generous with the curves for each exam. Attend (almost) all classes because he gives 2 questions in the beginning of class for attendance (but all graded if you at least did it, not necessarily the right answer). For his exams, mainly watch his lecture videos and take notes, and read the book.

analysis.name: Ty Climer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I don't understand why Professor Ty is getting all this hate. His class always was a great place to be at and the workload is really not that bad. I spent very little time working on the assignments given to me and passed with an easy A.
To be honest, if you do the homeworks and participate in the classes, it is an easy A (for SCLA110).

I would probably take Ty's class again. My biggest issue with his instruction was vague feedback that often went against what he would teach in class. He encouraged us not to heavily quote sources but would deduct points on assignments for doing just that. Even though I got an A, I disagreed with some of his reasoning for my grades.

Everything he does is quite unclear - He doesn't put rubrics on how he grades specific assignments and he's weird. And for some reason he thinks he's funny. I asked several times about where can I learn more about his grading policies and he didn't clear up any confusion. His classes are hella boring. Wouldn't recommend taking this weirdo's class.
he isn't that difficult unless you are just a lazy person he does kind of seem like a weirdo but hey his class is easy af

analysis.name: Colleen Delaney
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Delaney did an excellent job teaching MA366. Her lectures were extremely effective at explaining challenging content. Provided helpful example problems through her lectures to reinforce concepts taught. Extremely approachable outside of class for help in office hours. Exams were straightforward with no surprises. Highly recommend.

I took Ordinary Differential Equations with Professor Delaney, she was a great professor! Her lectures always explained the concept well and included excellent examples, which were great preparation for exams. She wrote extremely fair exams and if you have an understanding of the concepts being tested and practice enough, you will breeze through
Lectures are recorded and not required. Tests were graded very generously. HW wasn't that bad. The lab section for 366 (which is unrelated to prof) wasn't very good but is tolerable.

analysis.name: Congfang Huang
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Classes are monotonous and poorly prepared. The slides are often confusing and overtly abstract for rather simple topics. And, at times, it's very difficult to understand the professor's explanations. Grading is generous, but her teaching style is not. Would not take this class with this professor again.

Congfang genuinely cares about her students, especially when you are willing to discuss with her. However, I DO think Congfang needs a better preparation of the course, especially for teaching students materials in a logical and mutually understandable way. You might have to rely mostly on yourself for the course, although the grading is generous.

Congfang's IE 230 class is made up almost entirely of exam credit. There is barely any material to actively practice the topics covered in lecture. She is very hard to understand, which I know is not a fair criticism but it should still be taken into account. Her slides are just mindless info dumps with little to no analysis of the topics.

Grading Scale is pretty lenient, with an 84 being the minimum grade for an A. Not a lot of material, but it can be difficult to understand. This was her first time teaching, and it was at times difficult to understand. She has good exam reviews. Her review guide is very similar to the exam. She does genuinely care about her students/

The course material itself was fairly easy, but understanding the professor is a bit of a challenge. This was also her first time teaching the course, so maybe it was just a general nervousness or getting used to teaching the material. Prepare to teach yourself the material. Don't let this discourage you from taking this course.

analysis.name: Paula Conroy
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Paula was a very poor teacher. Her "lectures" used slides with many words/visuals that she would show for 20 seconds, never enough to take adequate notes. She would talk over each slide attempting to explain them, but it was hard enough to quickly type down the info, much less simultaneously process what she was saying.

great professor- lectures sometimes were long but if you study for the exam, you will get a solid grade in this class. homework was a little challenging because of the two different due dates with a total of 3 assignments. Although the assignments were extensively helpful. Extra credit every class- go to class you will pass the class.
Really bad and waste of time, you can learn nothing from this class

Terrible waste of time. Was waiting for her to retire but had to take the class to graduate before she did. Hope the school hires someone who can teach this class in an experiential way not a "memorize what a data set is" way.

Very big ego. The example questions have no answers on them, and I do not have enough storage to download every slide show and write the answer. She is also not very nice and likes to call people out.

analysis.name: Daniel Conner
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Conner is amazing. I very rarely rate professors, but I felt compelled to rate him. He LOVES Latin, which makes learning much more fun. Additionally, he's a very nice guy. Super understanding and easy to talk to. I recommend going to his extracurricular meetings (various classics related gatherings). They're a lot of fun.

Dr. Conner is by far my favorite professor thus far. He is extremely knowledgeable and intelligent and makes learning Latin an incredible experience. He is funny yet determined when it comes to his lectures. I cannot recommend his class enough.

Conner has been my favorite prof so far. He's really nice and funny, and turns boring PPTs into really great lectures. I like how much he cares about what he's teaching, he's so passionate about it that even if someone hated classics/greek mythology, they would still find his lectures interesting.I really hope I get to take another class he teaches

Took him for Latin 101 and 102, he was an amazing teacher who cares about the success of all his students. There is a crazy amount of homework, but in return the grading is quite easy. I would recommend his classes to anyone.

Prof. Conner is the only English or communications teacher whose class I have enjoyed taking. The assigned readings are easy, and he sets you up greatly for your papers. His feedback is incredibly helpful and makes the lectures fun. Frequent extra credit opportunity.

analysis.name: Steven Crain
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Crain was a great professor. He had a clear grading rubric for every assignment, taught us everything we needed to know to get an A, and gave good feedback. Everything was clear cut in his class. His lectures aren't boring and he keeps everything upbeat. He treated everyone respectfully even if they didn't do the same. Overall great guy.

Dr. Crain is the best lecturer I've had at Purdue and the best teacher I've ever had! He is very caring and genuinely cares about his students learning the materials properly. He offers a ton of extra credit and grades very fair. He provides lots of feedback on his grading so it is easy to learn and improve. I wish I could have him for every class.

Lot of work for what is a required course that most students don't care about. He gets this though and is extremely lenient with grading and time requirements and at least makes lectures worth showing up for.

Dr. Crain was wonderful. I was very nervous about taking this course, but he made it very easy and clear. He truly does care about his students doing well. He will work with you and your schedule, even asking students their availabilities before assigning presentation dates. If you're taking COM 217, please choose Dr. Crain if you can!

Dr. Crain is one of the best professors I have ever had at Purdue. He is provides great feedback on all speeches and has a genuine care for his students. He can be a tough grader at times, but gives plenty of opportunity for extra credit at the end of the semester!

analysis.name: Cheryl Crabill
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Mrs. Crabill has very clear and concise lectures, rarely talking about information that will not be gone over in exams. If she does do this, she always mentions what concepts you need to know. If you get a 75% or higher on iClickers, you get 3 extra credit points. Make sure to make cheat sheets for the exams because she encourages it.

Possibly my favorite professor I've had at Purdue. She loves her students dearly and enjoys her subject. The second exam leans more into applying the ideas taught in class to problems than actually asking you to list something. iClicker is for extra credit and the projects are sometimes fun but require a several-hour lock-in. Fantastic professor.

class is hard if you struggle in math calculations and good studying. The professor is great! there is iclicker which is annoying but if you have over 75% by the end of semester you dont have to keep going. projects are hard if you procrastinate. Must understand circuit or you'll lose easy points w peer reviews, must understand instructions clearly

I had a very positive experience in her class. She explains material clearly and creates a welcoming environment. Quizzes allow notecards, and exams permit a reference sheet, which helped me feel prepared. She encourages students to succeed and offers opportunities for extra credit. Overall, I found the course well-organized and supportive.

I passed STAT 113 with a B, but I would not recommend taking this class with this professor. Lectures were unclear, and exams differed greatly from lectures and practice exams, feeling more like a scare tactic than a fair test. The course needs clearer instruction, better alignment, and more support for new statistics students.

analysis.name: Colin William
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 102 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: William's lectures are super interesting! They can be information heavy and drag on (especially in the twice-a-week section), but his personality is engaging, and he'll often ask for student participation/examples. He loves answering questions and loves talking to students. Exams are fine, but you will def need to study both his notes and the book

i love him. lectures are engaging and hes funny but not mandatory. Four ~650 word discussion boards throughout the sem but aren't too bad-you can easily get max score on all of them if u js put in at least some thought into them. 4 exams but one is dropped. exams are prob the most challenging part of the course but arent extremely bad, just study

dr. william is the best professor. his lectures are so good i have literally walked to them super sick just because the class is so much fun and sometimes i forget i'm actually learning. his lectures are fun, easy to follow along, and straightforward. not mandatory attendance. exams and easy discussion boards. what else do you need? excellent guy.

He is very good at explaining confusing topics in clear and concise ways. He is able to break things down and make it easy for everyone to understand. Some of his lectures he would predominantly just read off of his slides but these were the small minority of lectures. It always felt like he wanted us to learn the material well.

I enjoyed this class and thought he was a good lecturer! Despite no tracked attendance I very rarely missed class. Sometimes his exams had some tricky questions but were overall very fair. I thought they were pretty harsh in terms of grading the paper but that did not stop me from doing well. I loved the class and would take it again!

analysis.name: Marta Crowe
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Mrs. Crowe is a great instructor and is always willing to help a student with any problem that she or he has.  I love this class and the way she handles the lectures because she really understands the material and what is happening in the course. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Took Marta for CS 177, and she was amazing. She was extremely accessible outside of class with basically 24/7 help available through all the TAs and herself. The labs have mandatory attendance but were the same as the prelab. Lecture videos were posted same day with the course participation being due at midnight that night.

Marta was very caring and overall the class was extremely helpful, however I find it much more beneficial to watch the lecture recordings instead of attending lecture because she moves really fast and if you have a Mac it is more complicating. There's a group project that lasts the whole semester and it is sort of confusing but graded very easy.

Marta is a great professor. Her lectures aren't mandatory, and you can always watch videos from class online. Labs are mandatory, but there is usually homework so it's a good time to get that done. A semester long group project takes up a big part of your grade, but it's nothing bad. Tests are long but as long as you did the HW you're fine.

Marta is a great professor. She is very clear in explaining things and wants her students to do genuinely well in her classes. The course was structured really well. It sucks that this is the last semester she is teaching this course. Overall, if you get her as a professor, you'll do well. Just make sure to do the work and ask questions.

analysis.name: William Crum
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 88 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I came into this class with zero coding experience and now I absolutely love it. Crum is a great lecturer and the homework assignments help one get a better understanding of the material, although they are very time consuming. At first the class seems impossible but if you put the time in to learn, youll do great. Oh and DO NOT CHEAT IN THIS COURSE

Horrible teacher. Exams had me on all fours especially with the MCQ as there was always the option for “none of the above”. Lectures are extremely content heavy and Crum teaches until the last second and CRAMS all the content he can. He has the lecture notes packet but never follows it so it gets confusing. Get another teacher🙏🏻🙏🏻

The class is very reliant on knowing advanced geometry always focusing more on geometry than actual coding. There are "course standards" that make everyone follow the same absurdly exact formatting. Miss a comment on one variable? Didn't like the name of a variable? Points off. Very very harsh graders (the TA's). DEFINITELY NOT an intro course.

I have never felt so defeated by a class before. I did not have much previous experience with coding and this is supposed to be an intro class. The labs and homework are difficult but they are worth basically nothing. The exams are very difficult and not like the assignments. They are also the majority of the points. Not easy to help. SI is a g.

Crum's full understanding of the C language is very apparent when he lectures. He explains concepts clearly and well. I loved him as a professor - I would have taken any other class that he taught. The exams and labs in this class are difficult, but Crum and the TA's are willing to help. Overall - Crum is a great guy and great professor.

analysis.name: Melba Crawford
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Crawford is a decent lecturer, though she tends to use language and terminology that surpasses what we have learned or what we should know for the exams. She has some really neat experiences in the field, and overall seems like a cool person. She does provide lots of good resources for the exam, but TAs will be your best resource when studying.

She is an ok professor, I think that I say ok because the content was pretty advanced and you have to play close attention and read the textbook to understand what is going on. She definitely knows what she is talking about, but with no prior experience in photogrammetry, it was difficult to keep up, but that might just be the course.

Mumbles sometimes, sit near the front.
Consistent with surprise quizzes
Really hard midterm not a whole bunch of study material either

Lectures are tough to understand. In class quizzes at least once a week. Exam was difficult as well, 40+ MCQ's and 7 Written Questions. Labs can be long and take significant time to complete. Labs also require software that cannot be installed on personal computer, requiring you to use software in computer lab.

Random in-class quizzes at least once a week. The exam consisted of around 40 multiple choices (worth 50% of exam) and around 3-4 pages of free response questions (worth 50% of the exam). Both parts of the exam were confusing. Not hard to get at least a C since the class is pre-curved, but the course is tedious.

analysis.name: Craig Voll
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: LOVE CRAIG! He is the HK dad! He starts class off with music and dad jokes! He loves what he teaches and is good at it. He actually makes me want to go to class, and enjoy it! Craig is very caring and supportive of all of his students. He strives to have a personal relationship with everyone. If you have a chance to take a class with him, DO IT!!

Professor Voll is an incredible professor. All of his students adore him and he is very personable to everyone. For example, before every class he plays music and says hello to every student who walks through the door, he usually knows them by name. He always has a smile on his face. I will be taking another class with him, he is amazing.
WE ARE DONE LIKE YESTERDAY'S DINNER
Professor Voll is a wonderful person.  This is my favorite class.  He gives out candy, and the class is actually entertaining.  Please take his class.
Amazing professor and person. He enjoys what he does and it shows!

analysis.name: Laszlo Csonka
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This man needs to retire. He is obviously knowledgeable about the subject but he is just an awful teacher. He reads off the powerpoint slides word for word in a slow, almost inaudible monotone voice so there was no point in even attending class. The powerpoints werent even good, so you often have to consult the textbook for clear answers.

Dr. Csonka is one of the worst biology professors as his teaching style is horrible as he only wrote on the chalk board with an outline given to the class. His tests are mostly application and he does class discussions that he randomly selects students to answer the questions. Students only knew 40% of their grade before it was on their transcript.

Dr. Csonka is simply a very bad instructor. I was disappointed to find that Biol 438 was co-taught by him and Dr. Applegate. Applegate was great, and it was a shame Csonka brought him down. Csonka doesn't really teach, he just very quietly reads off powerpoint slides. People stopped coming to his lectures because there was no point.

He's a really nice guy, especially if you're in one of his smaller (i.e. not the core bio) classes. He was very helpful with lab experiments in the class I took with him, and even did the experiments himself in case we messed ours up so we could see how it was supposed to turn out.

Dr. Csonka is an amazing professor. He is incredibly intelligent and cares for his students. He does have a thick accent which may be hard to hear through but it is able to be deciphered. Overall love him and would take his class again.

analysis.name: William Crossley
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Overall, the professor was excellent in the lectures and put in some effort to be available outside of class. Grading was usually fair and the regrade policy was generous. Flexibility in assessment and project due dates was extremely helpful and greatly appreciated. I would definitely take another course taught by this professor.

Interesting course, teaches non trivial topics very well as he puts in a lot of effort in the course. Only complaint is that feedback for homework takes a long time to get, dont expect to get feedback before the semester ends. But it's doable if you pay attention and try, just a lot of work. Recommend the course.

Content was good but course organization was very poor.

-Homework releases were routinely delayed or bugged, sometimes without notification

-Homework grading and feedback was terrible. Took about 2 months for the second homework to be graded, right before the last homework was due. No chance to make improvements because of lack of feedback.
He has all of his bad reviews removed from RateMyProf. Tells you everything you need to know

Took as an online student. Interesting material and fair grading. I'm not a big fan of his lecture style since it seems like so much of it is watching him fill in the notes. I'd rather have him focus more on the concepts/interesting tidbits/motivations since the math itself for MDO is pretty easy to follow on your own in general. Overall good class

analysis.name: Gabor Csathy
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He has a cool accent. Sometimes a little hard to follow but is usually pretty clear. Always checks clicker answers to make sure the majority of the lecture understands the topic and if the class is split or not getting it he goes into more detail. Seems to really enjoy the topic and teaching. All around a nice and good professor

With Gabor, the course really wasn't to difficult, essentially his lectures are from the textbook and he uses a lot of examples from the textbook and the practice exam. His exams are straightforward and relatively easy. Put in the effort and you should be able to get a good grade no problem.

He was just an OK prof.  All he did was read the lecture notes and besides the clicker points, there was no reason to go to class.   He was not the worst prof I have had here but definity not the best either.

Prof. Csathy's lectures can be dry to some, but he tries his best during demos and explanations. Physics is hard, but if you learn the lectures/ ppts., you'll be ok. Expect the following: 2 midterms (averages were 50% & 55%!!) and a final, weekly lab reports, weekly online homeworks, and iClicker participation. 7 - 8% curve at the end of the sem

He's one great guy!  His Romanian accent is awesome and just that alone sometimes made me want to come to class.  Explains things very well and you can fully understand him.  Some may just find the subject hard.  Although I said attendance was mandatory, it isn't, it's just that you have clicker questions you and get some points for being there.

analysis.name: Meng Cui
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Cui's lectures were very fast, but he did a good job explaining things and gave useful examples. Homework and exams had a few more difficult problems but were fair. My main issue was that we didn't have practice exams.

Cui is a great prof., he is very passionate and explains things thoroughly. However, he goes fast in lecture and has a thick accent so it is hard to understand him at first. The exams and material of 301 is very hard. However, prof. Cui is very inspirational, and works with students to help them understand the material.

He's an amazing professor for this class. He may have a thick accent and pretty bad handwriting, but he is so caring and really goes above and beyond to make sure every student understands. He goes at a good pace, goes over homework solutions and lecture reviews everyday, and he hand writes all of his notes (which I love). Great guy, I recommend!

Cui is a decent lecturer and I would consider him a safe choice if you don't have any good options. He has an accent but its not bad. His lectures are nothing special but he does a lot of practice problems which is nice, and responds via email decently quick, but wont care about any issues or conflicts you have, so expect no leniency.

He's not it. The lectures are the biggest waste of time. I have played an hour of clash royale in every single lecture this year. That being said, I know more about the material than anyone else I've met just because I only learn by myself. This means you only learn how not to do it by listening to professor Meng teach.

analysis.name: Thomas Cunningham
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: AAE 340 used a terribly difficult class. Prof Cunningham is improving it so that the material is learned thoroughly without making the content impossible. Lectures are very dry and not worth much, but homework is engaging and kind of fun. Exams are a time crunch but are graded generously. It is obvious that Prof Cunningham cares about his students.

Was not a good professor. Acts like he is caring and kind but will penalize grad students for working. Homeworks were 5+ hours and he didnt explain in lectures. He is a printing guy playing space. Run. RUN. RUN!!!

Cunningham is the GOAT. I had him for 203, 251, and now 450. Each time he made learning the material fun and, by extension, easy. He has unc status. He's that guy who is always looking out for you, but will challenge you in ways that make you grow. 10/10 professor and 10/10 person.

(shoutout Talaria and the entire Despicable Me franchise)

This is the quintessential Cunningham course. Very clear lecture style, first half of the course is a breath coverage of the spacecraft subsystems which can be a little dry if you are already familiar with them. Second half of the course is much more interesting coverage with failure analysis and operations procedure. Also very joyful person!!

Thomas Cunningham is who you want all your AAE professors to be like. Great notes, charming guy, and he makes a somewhat boring class (203) pretty interesting. Occasionally gives hints for HW and gives great tips for exams.

analysis.name: Alejandro Cuza
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Abysmal. I came into this class a fluent native speaker with C1 profiency and left feeling like I'd never encountered Spanish in my life. To this day I do not speak a lick of Spanish and find most episodes of Dora impossible to follow. DO NOT TAKE.
Heavy material but lighter grading, Meaning if you come prepared for tests you will do better than expected. Excellent class for improving Spanish.
Great professor, very funny as well. Participation does matter, easy A

analysis.name: Xingshan Cui
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Simply a lovely professor with care and consideration for his students as to what they need to know to succeed. His provision of relevant examples are incredibly important for understanding and while my grade may not reflect that, it is without a doubt that he is an excellent professor especially for showing critical 3-D shapes in relation to math.

Cui was a great professor overall. His lectures are very clear and help you understand the topics. He also goes over many of the upcoming homework problems which makes doing the homework easy to understand. Has great test review lectures. I knew many calc 3 students who had other lecturers that went to Cui's lectures instead.

Prof Cui has an accent and not the best handwriting, which I didn't really have a problem understanding after the first couple days, but if that is typically a problem for you, maybe consider a different lecturer. Overall, seemed like a nice guy, lectures were good, but exams were stressful.

His lectures follow Chenflix pretty closely and he keeps them lighthearted. Sometimes he stumbles on his words but he has good pacing in his lectures. You will be there for the full fifty minutes, he never ends early and sometimes fills with proofs not needed for the class.

Professor Cui did a very awesome job teaching calculus III. He goes over most of the proofs (though not required to know) which will help you understand where the equations come from. Lecture notes are always posted on brightspace after class.

analysis.name: Jason Cutter
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cutters Aviation Systems class might just be the easiest youll take outside Nolans AT10000 class. Theres one group presentation at the end of the course, and the tests are basically the study guides with answer choices. I had the 0730 slot and even though I sometimes fell asleep, I still had an A. If I can pass, you can too.

Pretty easy intro class with a couple of papers to write. Took less than 10hrs total over the whole semester to do, and 1/2 of the grade is just by following instruction on stuff like formatting and having a title page. Attendance is by QR codes at end of each class and they count towards the grade.

Dr. Cutter is very clear about the way he grades things and emphasizes the importance of communication. Gives good insight on the industry. The assignments consist of multiple papers that won't burden you as long as you start early.

Easy class. Grade is basically determined by turning in research papers and there are lots of extra credit points given out if you still somehow don't have an A. Speakers are interesting, but definitely a filler class for you to have more credits. Mandatory attendance.
Was transparent about grading criteria. Emphasizes communicating problems early and paying attention to instructions, which was not bad if you just put in the time. Overall easy class and professor.

analysis.name: Mark Cushman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Cushman is honestly like a 3rd grandfather to me. He is always super nice and checks in with students during lecture with clicker questions to see if "learning is occurring" and gives extra credit for these. His question on exams and quizzes were always easier and better understood than his counterparts questions. This man is my favorite.

This professor made me hate Purdue and pharmacy. Pray you never are required to speak to him. Im a quality student and I achieved my desired grade but this professor is terrible in understanding and speaking to students
daddy Cush is so cool I love him and he taught me a lot about organic things I am smart so I got an a+ but I can't say the same for others. -cc

Dr. Cushman cares about students' comprehension.  He gave quizzes before and after class (not for credit) to check on whether "learning was occurring."  He is also excited when you answer his questions correctly, pumping his fist and going "Yes!"

analysis.name: Tara Cuthbertson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof Cuthbertson is a very caring prof. She encourages group discussions a lot which can be good or bad depending on whether or not you're a person that likes that. I found her grading pretty fair. If you think she's a harsh grader she still gives a) tons and tons of feedback and b) allowed me to resubmit essays I did really poorly on.

Dr. Cuthbertson is probably the best professor I have ever had. She is caring, passionate, and very knowledgeable. Though she is a tough grader, she is more than willing to help her students and provides the means for them to succeed. Get ready to have a fun, philosophical, and mostly stress-free class!

Dr. Cuthbertson's class was a highlight of my week. She was always ready to make class fun but also a place where we could learn and ask questions. The class is based entirely around readings done outside of class, but they usually aren't super long. Participation is important and she'll try to get everyone to talk, even if it's only one thing.

The professor is very caring and understanding. She gives opportunities for extra credits and have a very fun personality. Participation matters a lot, you should contribute to class discussion semi-frequently to do well in class. I love that the books she requires for class is accessible, cheap, and have rich literary history and importance.

Other reviews said she was a strict grader, but she really was not. I got nothing lower than an 86 and I am a terrible writer. She cares lots about her job and even more about her students. She can talk for a while, but she encourages class participation, and it is nothing boring. She was probably by best professor this past semester.

analysis.name: Cynthia Koh-Knox

review_highlights.comment: PHPR 202 would be great if there were fewer people telling us what is important and what is not.  There is seemingly little communication b/t lecturers, so one cannot answer all the questions.

This professor relies heavily on the use of guest lecturers in her PHPR 202 course, making it difficult to find a consistent format.  I think she thought that using guest lecturers would give us more view points, but it was not helpful.  Also, study everything for her exam, even if she gives you "focus  points", because she may not stick to them.
Class is so easy, only one project and a few lecture reflections. Make sure to go for attendance. Easiest A of college for sure.
Eclectic individual with some great stories to share.
Could careless about nursing students. Uses a lot of guest lectures so she doesn't have to do anything. Not helpful. Did not stick to study guide.

analysis.name: Cynthia Fortner

review_highlights.comment: She's worthless when it comes to explaining homework assignments, essays, or any other important part of any college english course. I am an English major, and she made me consider changing majors because of her negative and unconstructive "feedback". I always made great grades, and was in AP English in high school, but she dropped my grade from a B to an F the 2nd to last class of the semester and told me to drop out-because I missed ONE class due to an emergency. HORRIBLE.

An amazing professor!  We did not have a "certain" textbook, but we did have to purchase three novels.  She can adapt the material covered in class with issues or subject matter, but maybe influential to the class.  She gives very positive feedback, extremley helpful, but she tends to get sidetracked.

She is the best professor I have ever had at Purdue. Sometimes she is not clear with her saying but it makes sense afterall.  she is very helpful and knows how to make an intersting class for her students.
She is so passionate!  It's infectious.  It's obvious she loves her work and that makes it easy for me to show up and do the work.  She likes student discussions and lets us create our own projects.

analysis.name: Justyna Czader

review_highlights.comment: SCLA101 is an easy course, with very doable work and an easy grade, but Dr. Czader herself is not a good professor. Easy course, but theres definitely better profs out there for SCLA101.

Listen, I respect a strict teacher. But she was beyond that, she would make fun of of other classes and would start conflict for stupid reasons. She has a problem admitting she is wrong at times, and her English could be better. Very monotone and seems like she hates her job. If you get her as professor, at the very least switch professors.

Unpredictable mood, can be strict, can be playful. Seems unapproachable though appears to want students succeed. Can be intimidating and doesn't hesitate to indirectly call out faults in front of the class.

99% of the professors at Purdue enjoy their job or at the very least treat you as their own. Czader does neither. Consistently mocks or is rude to students who have made genuine mistakes (in some cases for no reason at all), Goes on tangents trying to make points about something that has nothing to do with the assigned reading, makes up rules.. etc

I was on her good side, idk if this is due to my reading the syllabus/instructions or some other reason. She is fairly strict on grading with somewhat arbitrary rubrics, but if you put in effort and read the material, you can succeed. Once we got further into the semester, it became apparent she did care, but hard to tell with her behavior.

analysis.name: Dagne Hartman

review_highlights.comment: Never puts the same lecture slides on the board. Her exam questions are also always the hardest, and her content is never straightforward. Posts different lecture slides than the ones she presents. Out to get me I swear.

Worst professor in the history of education. Needs to be fired literally ASAP. Cannot teach, cannot critique, cannot even help students acclimate to a clinical setting; always criticizing NEVER constructively, always talking over patients.

analysis.name: James Davis

review_highlights.comment: Really good professor and you can tell he cares for the learning of his students. The lectures are very relevant. Big plus is that there are no exams or quizzes. However don't let that fool you as the class has a beefy workload at times with the group project, labs, solo project, and other assignments. If you take make sure you have time to devote.

Prof. Davis's lectures are incredible and there are a lot of connections he makes to the real world. He cares a lot about his students. However, the grading for the course is very slow given the amount of workload. Feedback is not given on time and grades have not been posted for anything, despite the end of the semester approaching.

No doubt at all, the best classroom experience I've ever had at Purdue. Dr. Davis does not teach in a "traditional" manner. He teaches his students in a result-oriented manner that actually preps you for the real industry/academia. He cares for his students, goes above and beyond to make sure that they make the most out of the course. Full points!
One of the best professors I've had at Purdue. Highly recommend taking any class offered by him

Davis was a pretty interesting professor for software engineering. He brought in several engaging speakers and has a lot of good experience and ideas to share. Classwork felt a little heavy at times and there wasn't a good way to rate groupmates who were behind on the project.

analysis.name: Cynthia Harwood
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: I do not think this professor is good at conveying her knowledge to students. She goes way too fast and all of my friends and I are very confused. The homework has nothing to do with her lectures, so you basically have to rely on google to assist you in completing problems.

Not helpful. Lectures are rambling, disjointed, and poorly timed. Often speeds through new and complex slides but spends excessive amounts of time on topics either too simple or too outdated to be applicable. Usually introduces the most important and complex concepts in the last 5-10 minutes of lecture. Good personality but class feels like a mess.

Decent lecturer, but for me, the book helped me more than she did. She would rush through lectures and would usually only cover the very basics of new material. For some reason I just could hardly stay awake in her lectures, even at 10:30. She was always available for office hours and was helpful then, but I found the book more useful in overall.

Not a shining star of Purdue's Profs, teaching a BEGINNER class and exam averages are in the mid 60's and will blame anything but herself. Don't bother going to class, she doesn't know how to do the examples either. She'll just confuse you. She's poorly prepared all the time and will do an example, say its wrong, then quit and leave you hanging.

Really just not a great teacher. Unclear about expectations, not helpful when asking for help, will not accept that her students failures are her fault. Don't expect going to classes to be helpful nor office hours, rely on the book only as she literally has no clue what is going on either. Does not fit in with the other professors at Purdue.

analysis.name: Daniel Johnstone
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: His teaching style is not the most exciting, but he the important bits across. If available, you should take Mummert instead, because he coordinates tests and therefore provides more up-to-date information. As a side note, Johnstone chews and drinks (dr. pepper and mountain dew) loudly in the microphone, which is a less than pleasant experience.

I didn't have many issues with him, he is open to criticism if he makes a mistake during a lecture and cares about his students. 

The difficultly comes from the exams and the quizzes. ChenFlix, Khan Academy, Professor Leonard (YT), and Paulsonlinemathnotes, were helpful in understanding the material. Hope you have a good TA and a big curve.

Prof. Johnstone was an incredible lecturer and makes abstract concepts understandable. The homeworks were long but the exams were forgiving. Make sure to read if you miss a lecture since the content builds on itself a lot. Quizzes could be resubmitted at any point for full credit, with VERY detailed feedback and hints. Overall a great class.

He teaches well enough that I did not have to review on Chenflix. I'm glad there are good lecture videos and no attendance is required. I don't think a "difficulty rating" is relevant for this professor because it's mostly the exams and TA graded quizzes which are the main difficulty points. Note that the homework takes a nonzero amount of time.

Johnstone is great. Lectures are super engaging. MA261 is very tough, so get ready for a LOT of out-of-class studying/prep. TBH, your grade in 261 heavily depends on your TA and exams. Johnstone is funny and simplifies concepts really well. His office hour sessions are also great. Take advantage of them! HW is heavy (2x/week) but doable. Good luck!

analysis.name: Daniel Kelly
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Super easy class if you choose to have graded participation: basically, miss less than 7 classes by the end of the semester, and receive additional 5% to final grade. Also, posts all lecture notes online, which literally covers EVERYTHING you could possibly need for papers and tests. Easy A for a PHIL class

Best professor on campus if you want to take a philosophy course. Let's you have an additional 5% if you miss less than 7 classes which was nice. Super lenient with grading the written essays and exams. He gives you a list of questions that could come for the exam and only picks questions from there which was nice.

Easily one of my favorite professors at Purdue! Very engaging lectures, clearly passionate about the subject, encourages class discussions, and very responsive. Class is well organized, reading quizzes are easy, 3 blue book exams are simple, 3 writing assignments are generously graded. Great class, even better prof. DMFK all the way!

He's a really smart and interesting guy. There are 3 or 4 papers each semester and 2 essay style exams. He presents the material in a clear and enjoyable way. All of the tests are based on his lectures and he doesn't post the slides online, so you must attend class. The material was interesting, but the course did tend to drag on towards the end.

Professor Kelly was my favorite professor throughout my time at Purdue. I really enjoyed the structure of the class. The discussions were easy to get into, the topics were interesting, the workload was not overwhelming. I ended up looking forward to this class because of how well he ran it and how stress-free it felt.

analysis.name: Daniel Nowak
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: take anyone but him for this class his requirements are not clear whatsoever and most of the assignments that we do in class has nothing to do with marketing management. he does not lecture properly and the exam is built on very niche things where he says that there maybe multiple good answers but we have to pick the best one AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS

Pretty harsh with grading, and there's lots of assignments that he never gets around to finishing so they just linger on Brightspace ungraded. You have to purchase access to this business simulation website for 60 bomboclat dollars and run trials with a team. He's chill most of the time but also incredibly unenthusiastic at presenting/lecturing.

Disorganized, unclear, and poorly run. Grades posted so late you never know where you stand. Midterm was 13 MCQ with 8 answers each in 20 min and felt designed to trick, not test. Teaching is outsourced to student debates and the syllabus totally ignored. Final project timing is unrealistic. Professor lacks basic course management skills. Avoid.

Very disorganized and difficult to learn from. Lectures are mostly random case studies with sloppy explanations and no slides or structured material to follow. It feels like you're teaching yourself most of the time. For a 7:30am class especially, the lack of organization makes it a waste of time. Would not recommend

Dr. Nowak is an awful professor. Do not take this class. He grades unfairly if you disagree with him, and missing more than two 7:30 AM classes drops you a letter grade. Most students scored under 40% on the midterm, and you must write a paper to get the curve. I would also like to say that 1-star reviews keep getting deleted- avoid at all costs.

analysis.name: Tamal Dey
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Highly recommend going to class. 381 is the hardest CS course I took and he was a brilliant professor and made all the concepts as clear as he could. Gave brilliant examples in class and always open to discuss after class. He is also really good about not making students feel bad if they don't get concepts and actually cares about students.

CS 381 was a time-intensive course, but Professor Dey was able to break down the concepts extremely well. He took time to answer questions during and after class, and he is very clear in what he is trying to say during the class. I also appreciated that he goes at a pace that is easy to keep up with during the lecture.

Lectures were engaging and he cared that students were understanding the content. The class itself is of course extremely difficult. Homeworks are time sinks and exams will be difficult to pass if you do not understand the content well. Definitely would recommend going to lecture

I took CS 182 with Professor Dey, and it was pretty good. Professor Dey really explained the contents well although the materials were not easy. He really understands what he is explaining. He is also fair and makes students involved during the lectures by making us think as much as possible. HWs were hard. Definitely enjoyed it when I look back.

1) He takes great interest in answering questions. He is very careful with answering them and follows up with students in the later lectures with even more details! Wow!
2) He puts emphasis on the points that are critical during lectures.
3) He also ecnourages and appreciates students for their class involvement and makes the lectures enjoyable.

analysis.name: Deb Henneberry
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed having Deb as a professor. She is very accommodating and will give extensions for pretty much anything. Do the work and you will pass the class. Every test is taken straight from FAA test questions so it helps you study for the written test. Towards the end the class becomes more like a study hall as people finish their written.

She is super super nice and really cares about each individual. The quizzes are the FAA questions which makes it clear if you need to study more. She'll extend your deadlines if you have some sort of issue. She'll tell engaging stories to help with the material. One of the best professors I've had hands down.
Incredibly knowledgeable and cares about the subject matter in the course.
Great teacher and prepared me well for faa written
She is the best lecturer at Purdue by far. Give her a raise!

Online - Whenever I asked about things I did not understand or inconsistencies between assignments and the course calendar, DP was incredibly rude in the responses - always told me to check it again and insisted that she had it right the first time.
Interesting class but she was not clear as to what she wanted in our assignments or papers. Has VERY different viewpoints.

Too much writing... Journals.. what the hell? I know we have to write in college, but JOURNALS?... I don't think so..And also since we're talking about Popular Culture and all that, we have to watch a bit more movies since everything is relevant. In the book we have a lot of references to movies, and yet we watched only 1 movie.
good teacher, however a bit unfair when it comes to assignments. On a personal level I really like her but as teacher she really grinds my gears.

analysis.name: Parveen Dhillon

review_highlights.comment: While this was Parveen's first semester teaching the course, I do hope he continues. He's very approachable and makes learning thermodynamics a bit less painful. Also hosted review sessions on weekends for the exams, which were very helpful. Overall, really cared about the students and their learning.

This was his first semester teaching, but he was outstanding. He was very approachable and cared about everyone's success. He is passionate about thermo, he brought things in to do live examples/show and tell for understanding. His lecturing is great, but when he runs low on time his accent is a bit hard to understand. Definitely a top 5 prof.

Even in his first sem teaching, he was a wonderful teacher. I actually enjoyed thermo conceptually because of him. analysis.name: Diana Zulli

Her lectures are interactive and interesting, and the material is genuinely interesting to think about. Overall, this was a great course and I hope you have the chance to take it with her.

I really enjoyed Dr. Zulli's lectures, she makes every class interesting despite what material she's covering. She is a fair grader and makes lectures fun. Definitely go to class, there are random participation activities and it's much easier to do in class than to do the homework.

really enjoyed this course, Dr. Zulli is so kind and made the material a lot of fun to learn

review_highlights.comment: Given the inherent difficulty of the course material, he does a fantastic job of relaying the information in a way that is easy understand and apply. Prof Milisavljevic is a great professor, he teaches the material very well, and answers all questions thrown at him in lecture. He also gives about 2-3 iClicker questions each lecture, and normally reveals the answer before closing the poll so most people get it right. He also explains that iClicker for those that don't understand.

Everything about him is great, except his teaching style. He goes way too fast, sometimes to the extend that you find it hard to catch up with the material and end up being confused. I have taken two classes with him and this has happened every time. Lectures very content heavy.

Dr. Milisavljevic is ADORABLE and INCREDIBLE! He makes physics so much easier (but it's still hard, FYI), and will actually make you laugh in class. iClicker questions are attendance points, but he is flexible if you need to miss a day for a good reason! Study the past exams and the iClicker questions (LIKE REALLY DO THIS) and you'll be fine!

Honestly, he's gotta be the best physics professor I've had yet. He does his best to help out as much as he can, keeps the mood light, and teaches the material well. He's a pretty funny guy and cares about his students. No complaints at all here, only praise.

analysis.name: Jeffrey Dick

Some leeway has to be given for CHM 224 being a new course, but the labs are BLOATED and the write-ups take a very long time. Jeffrey is a very talented lecturer, but it feels like his talent is wasted on the current curriculum. Exams are take-home and very easy. None of the material is difficult; The hardest part of this class is time management.

Jeffrey is a very caring professor and it is obvious that he wants his students to succeed. However, this class was a nightmare. I appreciate Jeffrey and his attempt, but it was not planned well enough. Labs didn't work, the write-ups were unnecessary, and the class was essentially intro to electrochemistry. Do not take if not required.

Dillman is a great guy and a great teacher. Being an aviation management major in a class thats mainly for flight students it was pretty boring, but Dillman did his best to keep the rest of us entertained.

The purpose of the course is kinda confusing. He basically lectures about a different part of aviation industry every class and all you have to do is write a brief summary. Lots of life and advice and a really chill and nice guy. Easy course to pass but pretty boring.

By far one of the best professors at Purdue. He wants you to learn, not simply absorb and then regurgitate the information. He is INCREDIBLY intelligent, and knows pretty much everything about anything.

The course I took was ancient western medicine and I had to WORK for my B. Very tough grader and values tons of detail. Tests were all made up of 10 short answer questions that had to be answered in 100 words minimum. This course took years off of my life.

analysis.name: William Dory

Other ratings seem unfair, easily the best class atmosphere compared to other classes this semester. Lectures can become a bit tedious at times for people that don't enjoy reading much, but Professor Dory is extremely knowledgeable and cares about what he does. analysis.name: Doug Pruim

Prof. Davis' teachings never follow any straightforward path. He often spends tens of minutes on tangents. Attendance is not taken, participation is sometimes tracked (seemingly randomly).

A fantastic instructor. Grades you according to your existing skill level, so if you put effort in you'll be fine.
This class was actually not bad. As long as you attend class everyday and participate you will be fine. She sometimes plays favorites but overall she is very sweet and a decent professor.
